01

大气之女与鸭蛋The daughter of the air and the duck's eggs

在最古老的时候，有一位少女，她是大气的女儿，名叫伊尔玛塔尔。她独自在空旷的天空中住了很久很久，渐渐觉得寂寞，就从天上降下来，落到了无边无际的大海上。狂风吹起了海浪，海浪使她怀了孕，她成了“水之母”，在海上漂流了七百年，却始终生不出孩子来。她向至高的天神乌戈哀求，请他来帮助她摆脱痛苦。不久，一只美丽的鸭子在海面上飞来飞去，想找一个地方筑巢，却到处找不到陆地。伊尔玛塔尔从水里抬起膝盖，鸭子以为那是一座小岛，就落在她的膝盖上筑了巢，下了六个金蛋，第七个是铁蛋。鸭子孵着蛋，伊尔玛塔尔觉得膝盖越来越烫，像要被火烧着一样，忍不住动了一下，蛋就滚进海里，摔碎了。可是蛋的碎片并没有消失：下半部的蛋壳变成了大地，上半部变成了高高的天穹，蛋黄变成了太阳，蛋白变成了月亮，蛋壳上的斑点变成了星星，黑色的碎片变成了天上的云。

In the oldest times there was a maiden, daughter of the air, named Ilmatar. She lived alone for ages in the empty spaces of the sky until she grew weary of it, and came down to the boundless sea. The wind raised the waves, and the waves made her with child; she became the Water-mother and floated on the sea for seven hundred years without giving birth. She cried to Ukko, the highest god, to free her from her pain. Soon a beautiful duck came flying over the waters looking for a place to nest, but there was no land anywhere. Ilmatar raised her knee from the water; the duck took it for a little island, built her nest on it and laid six golden eggs and a seventh of iron. As the duck brooded, Ilmatar felt her knee grow hotter and hotter until it seemed to burn, and she moved it; the eggs rolled into the sea and broke. But the pieces did not perish: the lower halves of the shells became the earth, the upper halves the high vault of heaven, the yolk the sun, the white the moon, the specks on the shells the stars, and the dark fragments the clouds of the sky.

Evidence / 证据《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第一章。claim.v0350.kal_1.01
02

万奈莫宁的诞生The birth of Väinämöinen

世界有了形状，伊尔玛塔尔又在海上漂了许多年，开始塑造大地的样子：她把手一指，就出现了岬角；用脚一踩，就有了鱼儿栖息的深坑；侧身一躺，就形成了平滑的海岸；她脚踏过的地方成了海湾，头枕过的地方成了港口。可是她的儿子还没有出生。万奈莫宁在母亲的腹中待了三十个夏天，又待了同样多的冬天，在黑暗中渐渐长大。他向太阳、月亮和大熊星祈求：请给我打开一条道路，让我走出这狭小的地方，去看看天空的太阳和月亮。可是没有回应。于是他自己用无名指推开了城堡的门，用左脚的脚趾拨开了骨头的门闩，从母亲的身体里爬了出来，一头扎进了海里。他在海浪中漂了好几年，终于来到一片无名的海岬，爬上了岸。这位后来被称为“永恒的歌者”的万奈莫宁，一出生就已经是一个老人了。

With the world given shape, Ilmatar floated on for many years and began to form the land: where she pointed her hand, headlands rose; where she pressed with her foot, deep pools for the fish were made; where she lay on her side, smooth shores appeared; where her feet touched, bays were formed, and where her head rested, harbours. But her son had not yet been born. Väinämöinen stayed in his mother's womb thirty summers and as many winters, growing in the dark. He prayed to the sun, the moon and the Great Bear: open a way for me out of this narrow place, that I may see the sun and moon in the sky. No answer came. So he pushed open the castle gate with his ring finger, slid back the bony bolt with the toes of his left foot, crawled out of his mother's body and plunged headlong into the sea. He drifted on the waves for years until he came to a nameless headland and climbed ashore. Väinämöinen, later called the eternal singer, was already an old man at his birth.

Evidence / 证据《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第一章。claim.v0350.kal_1.02
03

播种与大橡树The sowing and the great oak

万奈莫宁上了岸，看见大地光秃秃的，什么也不长。他请来播种者桑普萨·佩勒沃伊宁，让他在大地上撒下种子：山上种松树，山丘种冷杉，沼泽长桦树，低地长赤杨，湿地长柳树，河岸长稠李。树木都长起来了，只有橡树不肯发芽。后来一位从海里来的巨人帮忙，把一颗橡子种了下去，这棵橡树长得太大了，树冠遮住了天上的云，挡住了太阳和月亮，大地一片黑暗。万奈莫宁祈求母亲派人来砍倒它。海里走上来一个小小的男人，只有拇指那么高，穿着铜甲；可一转眼，他就长成了顶天立地的巨人，挥斧三下，把大橡树砍倒了，阳光重新照到大地上。接着，万奈莫宁开始种大麦。一只山雀告诉他：要先烧林开荒。他砍倒了整片森林，只留下一棵白桦，让鸟儿有地方栖息；一只鹰为此感谢他，替他打火烧林。他撒下麦种，向乌戈祈雨，大麦就长了出来。

Coming ashore, Väinämöinen saw that the land was bare and nothing grew. He called the sower Sampsa Pellervoinen to scatter seed over the earth: pines on the hills, firs on the knolls, birches in the swamps, alders in the lowlands, willows in the wet places, bird-cherries by the rivers. Every tree grew except the oak. Then a giant from the sea planted an acorn, and the oak grew so great that its crown hid the clouds and blocked the sun and moon, and the earth was dark. Väinämöinen prayed to his mother to send someone to fell it. A little man rose from the sea, no taller than a thumb, armoured in copper; in a moment he grew into a giant reaching the sky, and with three strokes of his axe he felled the oak, and the sunlight returned. Then Väinämöinen began to sow barley. A titmouse told him to burn the forest first. He felled the whole forest but left one birch for the birds to rest in; an eagle, thankful, struck fire to burn the clearing for him. He sowed the grain, prayed to Ukko for rain, and the barley grew.

Evidence / 证据《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第二章。claim.v0350.kal_1.03
04

约卡海宁的挑战Joukahainen's challenge

万奈莫宁的歌声和智慧传遍了四方。北方有一个年轻的歌手，名叫约卡海宁，听说有人唱得比他好，心里很不服气，不顾父母的劝阻，赶着雪橇去找万奈莫宁比试。两架雪橇在路上迎面相撞，缰绳缠在一起。约卡海宁开始炫耀自己的学问，说起鱼儿在哪里产卵、山上长着什么树、天地是怎样造成的，甚至说世界是他造的。万奈莫宁说：这些都是孩子和女人的学问，你所说的，你都不在场。约卡海宁恼羞成怒，要和他拔剑决斗。万奈莫宁不屑与他相斗，就唱起歌来。随着他的歌声，约卡海宁的雪橇变成了湖边的灌木，马变成了河边的石头，弓变成了水上的彩虹，箭变成了天上的鹰，他自己则一点点沉进了沼泽，泥水没过了腰，没过了胸，一直没到了下巴。这是《卡勒瓦拉》里有名的“唱歌比赛”：两位歌手比的不是力气，而是谁知道万物的起源；而在这部史诗里，知道一样东西的来历，就意味着拥有支配它的力量。

The fame of Väinämöinen's songs and wisdom spread far and wide. In the north lived a young singer named Joukahainen, who could not bear to hear that anyone sang better than he. Against his parents' warnings he drove off in his sledge to challenge Väinämöinen. Their sledges met head-on on the road and their reins tangled. Joukahainen began to boast of his learning — where the fish spawn, what trees grow on the hills, how heaven and earth were made — and even claimed that he had made the world. Väinämöinen answered that this was the lore of children and women, and that Joukahainen had been present at none of it. Stung, the young man challenged him to fight with swords. Scorning to fight, Väinämöinen began to sing. As he sang, Joukahainen's sledge became bushes by a lake, his horse a stone by the river, his bow a rainbow over the water, his arrows hawks in the sky, and he himself sank little by little into a swamp, the mire rising to his waist, to his breast, to his chin. This is the Kalevala's famous singing contest: the two singers compete not in strength but in knowing the origins of things, and in this epic to know where a thing came from is to have power over it.

Evidence / 证据《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第三章。claim.v0350.kal_1.04
05

用妹妹换回性命A sister for a life

约卡海宁陷在沼泽里，吓坏了，开始求饶。他说：放了我吧，我给你两张好弓；万奈莫宁不要，继续往下唱。他又说：我给你两条船；我给你两匹快马；我给你满盔的金子和满帽的银子；我给你所有的田地和庄稼。万奈莫宁都不要，泥水越升越高。最后，约卡海宁说：我把妹妹艾诺许给你，让她给你打扫屋子、烤面包、织布，做你的妻子。万奈莫宁听了，心里非常欢喜，就坐在一块喜悦的石头上，把刚才的歌倒过来唱了一遍，约卡海宁从沼泽里升了上来，马、雪橇和弓箭也都恢复了原样。约卡海宁垂头丧气地回到家，告诉母亲他把妹妹许给了老万奈莫宁。母亲却高兴地说：这正是我一直盼望的事，能有那位大智者做女婿。只有艾诺听了，坐在台阶上哭了起来。一个少女的婚事，就这样在两个男人的较量中被定了下来，而她本人一句话也没有被问过。

Sunk in the swamp, Joukahainen was terrified and began to beg. 'Let me go, and I will give you two fine bows.' Väinämöinen would not take them and sang on. 'I will give you two boats... two swift horses... a helmet full of gold and a hat full of silver... all my fields and harvest.' Väinämöinen refused them all, and the mire rose higher. At last Joukahainen said: 'I will give you my sister Aino, to sweep your house, bake your bread and weave your cloth, and be your wife.' At this Väinämöinen rejoiced; he sat down on a stone of joy and sang his song backwards, and Joukahainen rose out of the swamp, and his horse, sledge and bow returned to their own shapes. Joukahainen went home crestfallen and told his mother he had promised his sister to old Väinämöinen. But his mother was glad: it was what she had always hoped for, to have the great sage as her son-in-law. Only Aino, hearing it, sat down on the steps and wept. So a maiden's marriage was settled in a contest between two men, and no one had asked her a single word.

Evidence / 证据《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第三至四章。claim.v0350.kal_1.05
06

艾诺的命运The fate of Aino

艾诺到林中去折桦树枝做浴帚，在那里遇见了万奈莫宁。老人说：少女啊，不要为别人戴珠子和十字架，只为我戴吧。艾诺扯下胸前的十字架、手上的戒指、颈上的珠子和头上的发带，扔在地上，哭着跑回家去。母亲劝她不要哭，叫她打开阁楼上的箱子，穿上最好的衣服，戴上金银首饰——那都是母亲年轻时织的、留给她出嫁用的。艾诺却说：我宁愿嫁给大海里的鲑鱼，也不愿做老人的拐杖。她穿上最好的衣服，离开家，一连走了好几天，来到海边。她看见三个少女在海里洗澡，就脱下衣服，游到海中的一块彩色岩石上。岩石却沉进了海底，艾诺也跟着沉了下去，再也没有回来。一只野兔把消息带回了她的家。母亲哭了很久，她的眼泪流成了三条河，河边长出了三棵白桦，桦树上落下三只杜鹃，一只唱着“爱啊”，一只唱着“新郎啊”，一只唱着“欢乐啊”。诗中母亲后来悔恨地说：做母亲的人啊，千万不要逼女儿嫁给她不喜欢的人。

Aino went into the woods to break birch twigs for a bath-whisk and met Väinämöinen there. 'Maiden,' said the old man, 'wear your beads and cross for no one but me.' Aino tore the cross from her breast, the rings from her fingers, the beads from her neck and the ribbons from her hair, threw them on the ground, and ran home weeping. Her mother told her not to weep, but to open the chest in the loft and put on her finest clothes and her gold and silver — things her mother had woven and kept for her wedding when she was young. Aino said she would rather be the bride of the salmon in the sea than the staff of an old man. She put on her finest clothes, left home, walked for days, and came to the sea. Seeing three maidens bathing, she took off her clothes and swam out to a bright-coloured rock. The rock sank to the bottom, and Aino sank with it and never came back. A hare carried the news home. Her mother wept so long that her tears became three rivers; three birches grew by them, and on the birches sat three cuckoos, one calling love, one calling bridegroom, one calling joy. The mother later says in her grief: mothers, never force a daughter to marry a man she does not want.

Evidence / 证据《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第四章。claim.v0350.kal_1.06
07

鱼与失去的新娘The fish and the lost bride

万奈莫宁听说艾诺死了，日夜悲伤。他到海边去钓鱼，钓了很久，钓上来一条奇怪的鱼，它不像鲑鱼，不像鳟鱼，也不像任何他见过的鱼。他拿出刀来，想把它剖开做早饭，那条鱼却从他手里一跃而起，跳回了海里，在离船不远的水面上抬起头来说：我不是给你做早饭的鲑鱼。我就是艾诺，约卡海宁的妹妹，你想娶的那个少女。我本想做你的妻子，为你铺床、做饭，可你没有认出我来。说完，它就沉入了深海。万奈莫宁拼命撒网、垂钓，再也找不到那条鱼了。他悲伤地回到家里，觉得自己老了，再也没有欢乐了。这时，他已故的母亲从海浪下的坟墓里醒来，对他说：不要为约卡海宁的妹妹悲伤，到北方的波赫约拉去吧，那里有更美丽、更聪明的少女。

Hearing that Aino was dead, Väinämöinen grieved day and night. He went to the sea to fish and after long fishing caught a strange fish — not a salmon, not a trout, not like any fish he had seen. He took out his knife to cut it up for breakfast, but the fish leapt from his hand back into the sea, raised its head from the water near the boat, and said: 'I am no salmon for your breakfast. I am Aino, Joukahainen's sister, the maiden you sought. I would have been your wife, made your bed and cooked your food, but you did not know me.' Then it sank into the depths. Väinämöinen cast his nets and lines again and again but never found that fish. He went home in sorrow, feeling old and joyless. Then his dead mother woke in her grave beneath the waves and said: 'Do not grieve for Joukahainen's sister. Go north to Pohjola, where there are maidens fairer and wiser.'

Evidence / 证据《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第五章。claim.v0350.kal_1.07
08

约卡海宁的箭Joukahainen's arrows

万奈莫宁骑上一匹轻得像豆秆一样的马，踏着海浪向北方的波赫约拉出发。约卡海宁却一直记恨着沼泽里的耻辱。他做了一张钢弓，配上蛇筋一样的弓弦，削好了箭，蘸上了毒，埋伏在路边等着。母亲劝他不要射，说万奈莫宁是大地的歌者，他死了，世上的欢乐和歌声都会消失。约卡海宁不听。他射出第一支箭，飞得太高，射进了云里；第二支箭飞得太低，钻进了地下；第三支箭射中了万奈莫宁胯下的马。马倒下了，万奈莫宁跌进了大海，被风浪卷走了。约卡海宁回家得意地告诉母亲：我射死了老万奈莫宁。母亲说：你做了一件坏事，你射死了大地上最好的歌者。约卡海宁的母亲说得没错：在《卡勒瓦拉》里，歌声就是力量，也是世间欢乐的来源。好在这位“永恒的歌者”并没有死，大海托着他，像当年他出生时一样，把他带向远方。万奈莫宁在海浪中漂流，无依无靠，这时他已经离家很远，离北方的波赫约拉却越来越近了。

Väinämöinen mounted a horse as light as a pea-stalk and set off over the waves for northern Pohjola. But Joukahainen had never forgotten his shame in the swamp. He made a bow of steel, strung it with a string like a serpent's sinew, shaped his arrows and dipped them in poison, and lay in wait by the way. His mother begged him not to shoot: Väinämöinen was the singer of the land, and if he died, joy and song would vanish from the world. He would not listen. His first arrow flew too high, into the clouds; his second too low, into the earth; his third struck the horse beneath Väinämöinen. The horse fell, Väinämöinen tumbled into the sea, and the wind and waves carried him away. Joukahainen went home and boasted to his mother that he had killed old Väinämöinen. 'You have done an evil thing,' she said. 'You have shot the best singer on earth.' Joukahainen's mother was right: in the Kalevala song is power and the source of the world's joy. But the eternal singer did not die; the sea bore him up, as it had at his birth, and carried him far away. Drifting helpless on the waves, he was far from home and drawing ever nearer to the north.

Evidence / 证据《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第六章。claim.v0350.kal_1.08
09

鹰与洛希The eagle and Louhi

万奈莫宁在海上漂了许多天，又冷又饿，看不到岸。这时，一只巨大的鹰从天边飞来，它记得当年万奈莫宁烧林时为鸟儿留下了一棵白桦，就对他说：你曾经为鸟儿留下了栖息的树，现在我来报答你。它让万奈莫宁骑在背上，一直把他驮到北方的波赫约拉海边，放下他就飞走了。万奈莫宁在陌生的海岸上哭泣，哭声传到了波赫约拉的女主人洛希那里。缺了牙的洛希坐船来找到他，把他带回家里，给他吃喝，让他恢复了力气。万奈莫宁说他想回家。洛希说：我可以送你回去，还把女儿嫁给你，只要你为我锻造一件三宝：用天鹅的羽毛尖、不生育的母牛的奶、一粒大麦和夏天母羊的一缕羊毛把它造出来。万奈莫宁说：我不会锻造三宝，可是我家乡有一位铁匠伊尔马里宁，他锻造过天空的穹顶，他一定能做到。洛希答应了，给了他一架雪橇，叮嘱他回家的路上千万不要抬头看天。北方的波赫约拉在史诗里是一片寒冷而强大的土地，它的女主人洛希会魔法、有心计，后来成了卡勒瓦拉英雄们最难对付的对手。

Väinämöinen drifted on the sea for many days, cold and hungry, with no shore in sight. Then a great eagle came flying from the edge of the sky. Remembering that when Väinämöinen burned the forest he had left a birch for the birds, it said: 'You left the birds a tree to rest in; now I will repay you.' It took him on its back and carried him to the shore of northern Pohjola, set him down and flew away. Väinämöinen wept on the strange shore, and his weeping reached Louhi, the mistress of Pohjola. The gap-toothed Louhi came in her boat, found him, took him home, fed him and restored his strength. He said he longed to go home. Louhi said: 'I will send you home and give you my daughter too, if you will forge me a Sampo from the tip of a swan's feather, the milk of a barren cow, a grain of barley and the wool of a summer ewe.' Väinämöinen answered: 'I cannot forge the Sampo, but in my land there is a smith, Ilmarinen, who forged the vault of the sky; he can.' Louhi agreed, gave him a sledge, and warned him not to look up at the sky on his way home. Pohjola, the north, is in the epic a cold and mighty land, and its mistress Louhi, skilled in magic and cunning, becomes the hardest adversary of the heroes of Kalevala.

Evidence / 证据《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第七章。claim.v0350.kal_1.09
10

彩虹上的少女与斧伤The maiden on the rainbow and the axe

万奈莫宁赶着雪橇往南走，忽然听见头顶传来织布机的声音。他忘了洛希的叮嘱，抬头一看，波赫约拉的美丽少女正坐在彩虹上，用金梭银线织着布。万奈莫宁请她坐到自己的雪橇上来，跟他回家。少女说，要她跟他走，他得先做几件事：用一把没有刃的刀劈开一根马鬃，把一个鸡蛋打成看不出的结；剥下石头的皮，从冰上砍下木桩而不溅起一点碎屑。万奈莫宁一件件都做到了。少女又说：你还要用我纺锤的碎片造一艘船，不用手推、不用膝顶，把它推下水去。万奈莫宁在一块蓝色的石头上造船，可是恶灵希西和勒姆波暗中作怪，让他的斧头一滑，砍进了自己的膝盖。鲜血像河水一样涌出来，淹没了草地和山丘。万奈莫宁会许多咒语，却唯独想不起止住铁伤的那一首，因为他不知道铁的起源。

Driving south in his sledge, Väinämöinen heard the sound of a loom above him. Forgetting Louhi's warning he looked up, and there sat the beautiful maiden of Pohjola on the rainbow, weaving with a golden shuttle and silver thread. He asked her to come down into his sledge and go home with him. She said he must first do certain things: split a horsehair with a knife that had no edge, and tie an egg into knots no one could see; peel the bark from a stone, and cut stakes from the ice without splintering it. He did them all. Then she said: 'Build a boat from the fragments of my spindle and launch it without pushing it with hand or knee.' Väinämöinen set to building on a blue stone, but the evil spirits Hiisi and Lempo made his axe slip, and it cut into his knee. Blood gushed out like a river, flooding the meadows and the hills. He knew many charms, but not the one to stop a wound of iron, for he did not know the origin of iron.

Evidence / 证据《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第八章。claim.v0350.kal_1.10
11

铁的起源The origin of iron

万奈莫宁流着血，赶着雪橇去找能治伤的人。他走过一户户人家，最后在一座小屋里找到了一位白胡子老人。老人说：比这更大的伤我也治过。可你得先告诉我铁是怎么来的。万奈莫宁就讲起了铁的起源：最早的时候，三位少女在天上把乳汁洒向大地，黑色的乳汁变成了软铁，白色的乳汁变成了钢，红色的乳汁变成了生铁。铁害怕火，躲进了沼泽和泉水里，藏在狼和熊的脚印下面。铁匠伊尔马里宁找到了它，把它放进熔炉里锻炼，铁哀求他不要伤害它，答应永远不伤害自己的亲人。可伊尔马里宁在给钢淬火时，希西的鸟——一只胡蜂——飞来，把毒蛇的毒液、蚂蚁的酸液和蛤蟆的毒汁偷偷放进了淬火的水里，钢从此变得凶猛，背叛了誓言，连自己的兄弟都要砍伤。老人听完，大声斥责铁的罪恶，念起了止血的咒语，又派儿子去熬制药膏，替万奈莫宁包扎了伤口。伤口愈合了，万奈莫宁感谢乌戈，赶着雪橇回到了家乡。

Bleeding, Väinämöinen drove on in search of a healer. He passed house after house until, in a small hut, he found a white-bearded old man, who said: 'I have stopped greater floods of blood than this. But first tell me the origin of iron.' So Väinämöinen told it: in the beginning three maidens sprinkled their milk from the sky over the earth; the black milk became soft iron, the white became steel, the red became hard iron. Iron, afraid of fire, hid in the swamps and springs, under the footprints of the wolf and the bear. The smith Ilmarinen found it and put it into his furnace, and the iron begged him not to harm it, promising never to wound its kin. But as Ilmarinen tempered the steel, Hiisi's bird, a hornet, came and slipped the venom of serpents, the acid of ants and the poison of toads into the tempering water, so the steel became fierce, broke its oath and would cut even its own brothers. When the old man had heard it, he loudly rebuked iron for its wickedness, spoke the charms that stop blood, and sent his son to boil a salve, and bound the wound. It healed; Väinämöinen thanked Ukko and drove home.

Evidence / 证据《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第九章。claim.v0350.kal_1.11
12

锻造三宝The forging of the Sampo

万奈莫宁回到家，劝铁匠伊尔马里宁到北方去锻造三宝、娶波赫约拉的少女。伊尔马里宁说：我不去那个吃人的阴冷地方。万奈莫宁就唱出一棵开着花的冷杉，树梢上挂着月亮，枝间停着大熊星，骗伊尔马里宁爬上去摘月亮；等他爬到树顶，万奈莫宁唱起一阵狂风，把伊尔马里宁连人带树卷走，一直吹到了波赫约拉。洛希热情地款待他，问他能不能锻造三宝。伊尔马里宁找到一块石头砌起熔炉，叫奴隶们拉风箱，把天鹅的羽毛尖、母牛的奶、大麦和羊毛放进火里。第一天，炉中出来一张金弓，可它每天都要一颗人头，他把它折断了；第二天出来一艘红船，它专要去打仗；第三天出来一头金角母牛，脾气太坏；第四天出来一把金犁，专犁别人的田地，都被他扔回了火里。他唤来四方的风，风吹了三天三夜，三宝终于成形了，它有一个五彩的盖子，一边磨出吃的粮食，一边磨出卖的粮食，一边磨出存的粮食，每天各磨一大斗。洛希非常高兴，把三宝锁进波赫约拉的石山里，上了九道锁，三宝的根扎进地下九寻深。可是少女说她还不想离开母亲的家，伊尔马里宁只好垂头丧气地坐上洛希给的船，回到了家乡。

Back home, Väinämöinen urged the smith Ilmarinen to go north, forge the Sampo and win the maiden of Pohjola. Ilmarinen refused to go to that cold land that eats men. So Väinämöinen sang up a flowering fir with the moon in its crown and the Great Bear in its branches, and coaxed Ilmarinen to climb up and fetch the moon; when he reached the top, Väinämöinen sang up a whirlwind that swept Ilmarinen away and carried him to Pohjola. Louhi welcomed him and asked whether he could forge the Sampo. Ilmarinen built a furnace on a rock, set thralls to work the bellows, and put the swan's feather tip, the milk, the barley and the wool into the fire. On the first day a golden bow came out, but it wanted a head every day, so he broke it; on the second a red boat that wanted only war; on the third a heifer with golden horns, too ill-tempered; on the fourth a golden plough that ploughed other men's fields — all thrown back into the fire. He called the four winds, which blew for three days and nights, and at last the Sampo took shape, with a many-coloured lid; on one side it ground grain for eating, on another for selling, on a third for storing, a great measure each day. Louhi rejoiced and locked the Sampo in the stone mountain of Pohjola behind nine locks, its roots sunk nine fathoms deep. But the maiden said she would not yet leave her mother's house, and Ilmarinen went home crestfallen in the boat Louhi gave him.

Evidence / 证据《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第十章。claim.v0350.kal_1.12

Editorial boundary / 编辑边界

依据克劳福德 1888 年英译《卡勒瓦拉》第一至十章，按诗章顺序讲述。《卡勒瓦拉》是隆洛特在十九世纪根据芬兰与卡累利阿的民间口传诗歌编成的史诗，与民间原始唱本并不完全相同；本篇讲述的是隆洛特的编排。克劳福德的人名拼写（如 Wainamoinen、Pohyola）已改为现代通行拼法。

芬兰 / Finnish

卡勒瓦拉 · 第二部 勒明凯宁Kalevala, Part 2: Lemminkäinen

英俊而鲁莽的勒明凯宁从萨里岛抢走了少女基利基，两人立誓：他不再去打仗，她不再去村里跳舞。基利基破了誓，勒明凯宁就要到北方的波赫约拉去另求新娘。母亲苦苦相劝，他把梳子往墙上一掷，说：梳子流血的时候，就是我遭难的时候。他在波赫约拉用歌声赶走了所有的巫师，只放过了一个又老又瞎、被他嘲笑的牧人。洛希给他出了三道难题：滑雪追捕希西的麋鹿，给希西喷火的马套上笼头，射死图奥内拉黑河上的天鹅。前两件他都做到了，第三件时，那个盲眼牧人在河边用一条水蛇刺穿了他的心，把他抛进黑河，亡者之王的儿子把他砍成了碎块。家中的梳子流出了血。母亲赶到北方，从洛希和太阳那里问出真相，请铁匠打了一把长柄铜耙，从黑河里一块块捞出儿子的身体，缝合血脉，又派蜜蜂从九重天外取来神的蜜膏，终于让儿子活了过来。

The handsome, reckless Lemminkäinen carries off the maiden Kyllikki from the island of Saari, and they vow — he never to go to war, she never to go dancing in the village. When she breaks her vow, he sets out for northern Pohjola to woo another. His mother begs him to stay; he flings his brush at the wall: when it bleeds, misfortune has befallen me. In Pohjola he sings all the sorcerers away but spares an old blind herdsman, whom he mocks. Louhi sets him three tasks: to catch the elk of Hiisi on skis, to bridle Hiisi's fire-breathing horse, and to shoot the swan on the black river of Tuonela. He does the first two; at the third, the blind herdsman pierces his heart with a water-serpent and throws him into the river, where the son of the lord of the dead hews him to pieces. At home the brush drips blood. His mother hurries north, learns the truth from Louhi and the sun, has the smith forge a long-handled copper rake, gathers her son's body piece by piece from the river, joins his veins, and sends a bee beyond the nine heavens for the Creator's honey, until her son lives again.

01

萨里岛的花The flower of Saari

勒明凯宁又叫阿赫蒂、考科米耶利，是一个英俊的年轻人，脸颊红润，头发漂亮，可是性情放荡不羁，眼睛总是在少女们身上打转。他听说萨里岛上有一位美丽的少女，名叫基利基，被称为“萨里岛之花”，许多求婚者——太阳的儿子、月亮的儿子、星星的儿子，甚至遥远国度的王子——都被她拒绝了。勒明凯宁不顾母亲的劝阻，赶着雪橇来到萨里岛。岛上的少女们嘲笑他，说他是个穷小子，连马都喂不饱。勒明凯宁并不生气，他留在岛上，白天和少女们一起玩耍，晚上和她们一起跳舞，很快就和岛上所有的少女都成了朋友，只有基利基一个人对他不理不睬，从不正眼看他。可是勒明凯宁已经下定了决心：非娶到这朵萨里岛之花不可。他的另一个名字考科米耶利，意思是“心在远方的人”，正好说明了他的性情：他永远不肯安安稳稳地待在家里。母亲曾警告他，萨里岛的人会看不起一个外乡来的穷小子，可他偏偏要去试一试。

Lemminkäinen, also called Ahti and Kaukomieli, was a handsome young man with ruddy cheeks and fine hair, but wild and reckless, his eyes always roving after the maidens. He heard that on the island of Saari lived a beautiful maiden named Kyllikki, called the flower of Saari, who had refused many suitors — the son of the sun, the son of the moon, the son of the stars, even princes from distant lands. Against his mother's warnings he drove his sledge to Saari. The island maidens mocked him as a poor fellow who could not even feed his horse. He did not take offence; he stayed on the island, played with the maidens by day and danced with them by night, and soon was friends with every maiden there — except Kyllikki, who would not even look at him. But Lemminkäinen had made up his mind: he would have the flower of Saari. His other name, Kaukomieli, means far-minded, and it fits him: he could never stay quietly at home. His mother had warned him that the people of Saari would look down on a poor stranger, but he had to try.

Evidence / 证据《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第十一章。claim.v0350.kal_2.01
02

雪橇上的新娘The bride in the sledge

有一天傍晚，少女们在林间空地上跳舞，基利基跳在最前面。勒明凯宁赶着雪橇冲过来，一把抱起基利基，把她扔进雪橇，用鞭子一甩，飞驰而去。基利基又哭又喊，求他放她回家，说：放我回去吧，不然我就喊我的兄弟们来，他们会追上你，把你的头砍下来。勒明凯宁说：我的心是勇敢的，我的剑是锋利的，我不怕你的兄弟。基利基哭着说，他是一个只会打仗的穷汉。勒明凯宁就向她许诺：我发誓，从今以后再也不去打仗，哪怕金银堆成山也不去。你也要发誓，从今以后不再到村子里去跳舞，不管多么想去。基利基答应了。两人在乌戈面前立下誓约，回到勒明凯宁的家。母亲欢喜地迎接了这位美丽的儿媳。这两个誓言把两个性情相反的人拴在一起：一个是好斗的英雄，一个是爱热闹的少女。誓言立下了，危险却也一起埋下了。

One evening the maidens were dancing in a forest glade with Kyllikki leading them. Lemminkäinen drove up in his sledge, seized Kyllikki, threw her into the sledge, cracked his whip and sped away. Kyllikki wept and cried out, begging to be let go home: 'Let me go, or I will call my brothers; they will overtake you and cut off your head.' He answered: 'My heart is brave and my sword is sharp; I do not fear your brothers.' She wept that he was a poor man who only knew how to fight. So he promised her: 'I swear never again to go to war, not even for mountains of gold and silver. And you must swear never again to go dancing in the village, however much you long to.' Kyllikki agreed. They swore their oaths before Ukko and went to Lemminkäinen's home, where his mother joyfully welcomed her beautiful daughter-in-law. The two vows bound together two people of opposite nature, a quarrelsome hero and a maiden who loved merrymaking; with the vows, the danger too was laid down.

Evidence / 证据《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第十一章。claim.v0350.kal_2.02
03

破誓The broken vow

日子一天天过去，勒明凯宁常常出门去打鱼。有一天他出海很晚还没有回来，基利基一个人在家闷得慌，就违背誓言，偷偷跑到村子里去跳舞了。勒明凯宁的妹妹艾尼基看见了，等哥哥一回来，就把这件事告诉了他。勒明凯宁又气又恼，说：基利基破了她的誓言，那我也不必再守我的誓言了。我要去打仗，我要到北方的波赫约拉去，向那里的少女求婚。基利基哭着请求原谅，他却已经铁了心。他对母亲说：快把我的战衣拿来，把我的剑拿来，我要到波赫约拉去，那里有美丽的少女，还有许多巫师等着我去较量。一个誓言的破灭，就这样把这位英雄重新推上了危险的道路。艾尼基告诉哥哥的话很简单：基利基到别人的村子里去了，在那里和人一起跳舞。这一句话，就让勒明凯宁觉得自己也被誓言解脱了。母亲劝他说，誓言是两个人一起立的，破了一半也还剩一半，可他已经听不进去了。

The days went by, and Lemminkäinen often went out fishing. One day he stayed out late on the water, and Kyllikki, weary of being alone at home, broke her vow and slipped off to the village to dance. Lemminkäinen's sister Ainikki saw her and told her brother as soon as he came home. Angry and hurt, he said: 'Kyllikki has broken her oath, so I need not keep mine. I will go to war; I will go north to Pohjola and woo a maiden there.' Kyllikki wept and begged forgiveness, but his mind was made up. He said to his mother: 'Bring my war-coat, bring my sword. I am going to Pohjola, where there are beautiful maidens and many sorcerers waiting for me to match my strength against them.' So the breaking of one vow set the hero back on the road of danger. Ainikki's words to her brother were simple: Kyllikki has gone to a strange village and danced there. That one sentence was enough for Lemminkäinen to think himself released from his own oath. His mother said that the vow had been made by two and half of it still stood, but he would not hear her.

Evidence / 证据《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第十二章。claim.v0350.kal_2.03
04

流血的梳子The bleeding brush

母亲苦苦劝他：不要去波赫约拉，那里的拉普兰巫师会用歌声把你唱进火里、唱进冰里，你一个人去会丢掉性命的。勒明凯宁说：拉普兰的巫师们早就对我唱过歌了，我一点也不怕。母亲说：你有一个美丽的妻子在家，还要去别处找什么新娘？他不听，梳好了头，把梳子往墙上——一说是往炉边——一扔，说：当这把梳子流出血来的时候，就是我遭到不幸的时候。母亲和妻子哭着看他穿上铁甲，佩上宝剑，套好了马，赶着雪橇向北方出发了。他一路上念着咒语，祈求乌戈和森林的神灵保佑他，给他的剑和马增添力量。那把留在家中的梳子，从此成了母亲日夜守望的信号。在整部史诗里，勒明凯宁的母亲是最坚定、最勇敢的人物之一。儿子离开的那一刻，她就开始守望；后面的故事会证明，她的爱比亡者之河还要深。勒明凯宁却头也不回，他的心思已经全在北方。

His mother begged him: 'Do not go to Pohjola. The Lapland sorcerers will sing you into fire and ice; alone you will lose your life.' He answered: 'The Lapland sorcerers have sung against me before; I do not fear them.' 'You have a beautiful wife at home,' she said. 'Why seek a bride elsewhere?' He would not listen. He combed his hair and flung the brush against the wall — or by the stove, in some tellings — and said: 'When this brush drips blood, misfortune has befallen me.' His mother and wife wept as he put on his iron mail, girded his sword, harnessed his horse and drove off north. All the way he chanted charms, praying Ukko and the spirits of the forest to guard him and give strength to his sword and horse. The brush left at home became the sign his mother watched day and night. In the whole epic Lemminkäinen's mother is one of the most steadfast and courageous figures. From the moment her son left she began to watch; the story will show that her love runs deeper than the river of the dead. Lemminkäinen never looked back; his mind was already in the north.

Evidence / 证据《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第十二章。claim.v0350.kal_2.04
05

巫师与盲牧人The sorcerers and the blind herdsman

勒明凯宁来到波赫约拉，走进洛希的大厅，那里坐满了巫师和歌者，弹琴的弹琴，唱歌的唱歌。他们看见这个陌生人，都不理睬他。勒明凯宁就站在门口唱起歌来，歌声像火一样从他口中喷出，他把那些巫师一个个唱走了：有的唱进了荒野，有的唱进了湖里，有的唱进了激流，有的唱到了冰封的远方。最后，大厅里只剩下一个又老又瞎、戴着湿帽子的牧人，叫马尔卡哈图。勒明凯宁没有对他唱歌，反而嘲笑他说：你这个可怜的老头，我才不屑对你唱，你又瞎又丑，连自己的姐妹都敢欺负，连牛都看不好。老牧人受了这番羞辱，心里怀恨，悄悄走出大厅，来到图奥内拉的黑河边，等着勒明凯宁总有一天会从这里经过。马尔卡哈图这个名字，意思是“湿帽子”。勒明凯宁唱走了所有强大的对手，却偏偏轻视了这个最不起眼的老人，这一次轻视，后来要了他的命。

Arriving in Pohjola, Lemminkäinen went into Louhi's hall, which was full of sorcerers and singers playing and singing; they ignored the stranger. He stood in the doorway and began to sing, and song poured from his mouth like fire. He sang the sorcerers away one by one: some into the wilderness, some into the lakes, some into the rapids, some to icebound distant places. At last only one was left in the hall, an old, blind herdsman in a wet hat, named Märkähattu. Lemminkäinen did not sing against him but mocked him: 'You wretched old man, I would not stoop to sing against you; you are blind and ugly, you have wronged your own kin and cannot even tend the cattle.' Shamed and full of hatred, the old herdsman slipped out of the hall, went to the black river of Tuonela, and waited there for the day Lemminkäinen would pass that way. The name Märkähattu means Wet-hat. Lemminkäinen sang away all his mighty rivals but slighted the humblest old man of all, and that slight would cost him his life.

Evidence / 证据《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第十二章。claim.v0350.kal_2.05
06

希西的麋鹿The elk of Hiisi

勒明凯宁向洛希求娶她的女儿。洛希说：你已经有妻子了，可要是你能滑雪捉住希西的麋鹿，我就把女儿给你。勒明凯宁找到一个造雪橇板的巧匠，请他做了一副好滑雪板，一边做一边夸口：森林里没有一只野兽能逃过我的滑雪板。恶灵希西听见了，就用朽木、柳枝、草根和沼泽里的东西造出一头麋鹿，让它奔向拉普兰。勒明凯宁滑着雪追了上去，滑雪板在雪地上嘶嘶作响，像火一样飞快。那头麋鹿一路狂奔，冲进拉普兰人的家里，踢翻了锅子，弄得煮好的肉都掉进了灰里，拉普兰的妇女和孩子又哭又笑。勒明凯宁用力过猛，一脚踩下去，滑雪板啪的一声折断了，滑雪杖也断了，麋鹿逃得无影无踪。他站在雪地里，心里懊恼极了。为他做滑雪板的巧匠，原诗里叫考皮，又叫吕利基。希西是史诗里的恶灵，常常和另一个恶灵勒姆波一起，给英雄们制造麻烦。

Lemminkäinen asked Louhi for her daughter. Louhi said: 'You have a wife already, but if you can catch the elk of Hiisi on skis, my daughter shall be yours.' He went to a skilled maker of skis and had a fine pair made, boasting as they were made that no beast in the forest could escape his skis. The evil spirit Hiisi heard, and made an elk out of rotten wood, willow twigs, roots and things of the swamp, and set it running towards Lapland. Lemminkäinen sped after it on his skis, which hissed over the snow as swift as fire. The elk ran wild, burst into the Lapps' huts and kicked over their kettles so that the meat fell into the ashes, and the Lapp women and children wept and laughed. Lemminkäinen thrust down so hard that his ski snapped, and his ski-pole too, and the elk vanished. He stood in the snow, bitterly vexed. The ski-maker is called in the poem Kauppi, also Lyylikki. Hiisi is an evil spirit of the epic, often paired with another, Lempo, in making trouble for the heroes.

Evidence / 证据《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第十三章。claim.v0350.kal_2.06
07

森林之神The gods of the forest

勒明凯宁修好了滑雪板，这一次他不再夸口，而是向森林之神祈祷。他向森林之王塔皮奥和森林女主人米耶利基唱起祈祷的歌：森林的主人啊，美丽的森林之母啊，请打开你的金库，把那头麋鹿赶到我的路上来，我会用金子和银子报答你。他唱森林的美丽，唱森林之母穿着金色的衣裙，唱树木像盛装的人一样站立。他一连祈祷了三天，森林之神被他的歌声感动了，把那头麋鹿赶到了他面前。勒明凯宁终于捉住了希西的麋鹿，把它带回波赫约拉交给洛希，说：我已经做到了，把女儿给我吧。可是洛希又提出了第二个难题。在原诗里，这些祈祷占了很长的篇幅，保留了古代芬兰猎人向森林神灵祈求猎物的祷词；塔皮奥的国度叫塔皮奥拉，是森林中一个富足的王国。这一次，勒明凯宁靠的不是夸口，而是谦卑的祈求。

Lemminkäinen mended his skis, and this time, instead of boasting, he prayed to the forest gods. He sang to Tapio, king of the forest, and Mielikki, its mistress: 'Master of the forest, fair mother of the woods, open your treasure-house and drive that elk into my path, and I will repay you with gold and silver.' He sang of the beauty of the forest, of its mother in golden garments, of the trees standing like people in festive dress. For three days he prayed, and the forest gods, moved by his song, drove the elk to him. At last he caught the elk of Hiisi, brought it to Pohjola and gave it to Louhi: 'I have done it; give me your daughter.' But Louhi set him a second task. In the poem these prayers run long, preserving the words with which old Finnish hunters asked the forest spirits for game; Tapio's realm, Tapiola, is a rich kingdom in the forest. This time Lemminkäinen succeeded not by boasting but by humble prayer.

Evidence / 证据《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第十四章。claim.v0350.kal_2.07
08

火焰之马The fire-breathing horse

洛希说：你去把希西那匹棕色的骟马套上笼头，它在希西的原野上奔跑，鼻孔里喷着火，嘴里冒着烟。勒明凯宁带着金笼头和银马勒出发了。那匹马奔过来，鼻孔里喷出的火焰让人无法靠近。勒明凯宁向乌戈祈求：至高的乌戈啊，请降下冰雹和雪雨，落在这匹烈马的身上，浇灭它的火焰。乌戈降下了铁一样的冰雹，那匹马被冰雹浇灭了身上的火，勒明凯宁趁机走上前去，用温和的话哄它：好马啊，不要伤害我，低下你的头来，套上这金色的笼头吧，我不会用鞭子抽你。马低下了头，他给它套上了笼头，骑着它回到了波赫约拉。可洛希还是不肯把女儿给他，又说出了第三个难题，这一次的地方，比前两次都要可怕得多。这一次，他又一次学会了不靠蛮力，而是靠祈求和温和的话语。

Louhi said: 'Go and bridle the brown gelding of Hiisi, which runs on Hiisi's meadows breathing fire from its nostrils and smoke from its mouth.' Lemminkäinen set out with a golden halter and a silver bridle. The horse came galloping, and the flames from its nostrils let no one near. Lemminkäinen prayed: 'Highest Ukko, send down hail and sleet on this wild horse and quench its fire.' Ukko sent down hail like iron, the fire on the horse was quenched, and Lemminkäinen stepped up and coaxed it gently: 'Good horse, do not harm me; bow your head into this golden halter. I will not strike you with the whip.' The horse bowed its head; he bridled it and rode back to Pohjola. Still Louhi would not give him her daughter, and named a third task, in a place far more terrible than the first two. Once again he succeeded not by force but by prayer and gentle words.

Evidence / 证据《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第十四章。claim.v0350.kal_2.08
09

图奥内拉的天鹅The swan of Tuonela

洛希说：你去图奥内拉的黑河上，只射一箭，射死那里的天鹅，我就把女儿给你。图奥内拉是亡者之地，那条黑河就在亡者之王图奥尼的国度里。勒明凯宁背着弓箭，来到黑河边的瀑布旁，等着天鹅游过来。可是那个被他嘲笑过的盲眼牧人马尔卡哈图早就埋伏在河边了。他看见勒明凯宁走来，就从河水里抓起一条水蛇，像投矛一样投过去，水蛇穿过了勒明凯宁的左腋，刺穿了他的心脏和右肩。勒明凯宁倒在地上，痛苦地说：我真是疏忽啊，我没有问过母亲，没有学会对付水蛇的咒语。我知道三条咒语，却唯独不知道这一条。如果母亲在身边，她一定会告诉我该怎么办。这只在亡者之河上游动的天鹅，后来成了芬兰艺术中有名的形象，作曲家西贝柳斯的交响诗《图奥内拉的天鹅》就取材于此。

Louhi said: 'Go to the black river of Tuonela, and with a single arrow shoot the swan there; then my daughter shall be yours.' Tuonela was the land of the dead, and the black river lay in the realm of Tuoni, lord of the dead. Lemminkäinen took his bow and arrows and went to the falls of the black river to wait for the swan. But the blind herdsman Märkähattu, whom he had mocked, lay in wait by the river. Seeing Lemminkäinen come, he drew a water-serpent from the river and hurled it like a spear; it passed under Lemminkäinen's left arm and through his heart and out at his right shoulder. Lemminkäinen fell and said in his agony: 'I was careless: I never asked my mother, never learned the charm against the water-serpent. I knew three charms but not this one. If my mother were here, she would tell me what to do.' The swan swimming on the river of the dead became a famous image in Finnish art; Sibelius's tone poem The Swan of Tuonela takes its subject from here.

Evidence / 证据《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第十四章。claim.v0350.kal_2.09
10

黑河里的碎片The pieces in the black river

盲眼牧人把奄奄一息的勒明凯宁扔进了图奥内拉的黑河里，河水把他卷向汹涌的瀑布。亡者之王图奥尼的儿子——一个满身血污的人——站在河里，拿着刀把勒明凯宁砍成了好几块，扔进了图奥内拉深深的河水里，说：你就在这里躺着吧，带着你的弓和箭，去射河上的天鹅吧。一位英雄就这样消失在亡者之河的深处，没有坟墓，也没有人知道他的下落。远方的家中，母亲和妻子还在等着他回来。这一章短促而阴暗，诗人只用几句话就交代了勒明凯宁的死，仿佛连诗歌本身也不愿在这黑河边多停留一刻。可是在《卡勒瓦拉》里，死亡并不总是故事的终点。原诗把图奥尼的儿子称为“血红的图奥尼之子”。那只天鹅仍在黑河上静静地游着，没有人射中它。

The blind herdsman threw the dying Lemminkäinen into the black river of Tuonela, and the current swept him towards the roaring falls. The son of Tuoni, lord of the dead — a man stained with blood — stood in the river with a knife, hewed Lemminkäinen into pieces and threw them into the deep waters of Tuonela, saying: 'Lie there with your bow and arrows, and shoot the swan on the river.' So the hero vanished into the depths of the river of the dead, with no grave, and no one knowing where he lay. Far away at home his mother and wife still waited for him. The rune is brief and dark; the singer tells Lemminkäinen's death in a few lines, as if the song itself would not linger by that black river. But in the Kalevala death is not always the end of the story. The poem calls him the bloody son of Tuoni. The swan still swam quietly on the black river; no one had shot it.

Evidence / 证据《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第十四章。claim.v0350.kal_2.10
11

母亲的寻找The mother's search

在勒明凯宁的家里，母亲每天都看着那把梳子。有一天，梳子上忽然渗出了血。母亲大哭起来，立刻提起裙子，一路奔向北方。她来到波赫约拉，逼问洛希：我的儿子在哪里？洛希先说给了他一匹马，又说让他去打猎了。母亲说：你在撒谎！快说实话，不然我就毁掉你的仓库，打碎你的三宝。洛希这才说出，她派勒明凯宁去射图奥内拉的天鹅。母亲到处寻找，她问树木，树木说：我们自己的苦已经够多了，没有看见你的儿子；她问道路，道路说：我被人踩、被车轧，没有看见；她问月亮，月亮也说不知道。最后她问太阳，太阳说：你的儿子在图奥内拉的黑河里，他被砍成了碎块，沉在河底。太阳高高在天上，什么都看得见，所以只有它知道真相。母亲听了，不再哭泣，而是转身去找能帮她把儿子捞上来的人。

At home, Lemminkäinen's mother watched the brush every day. One day blood suddenly oozed from it. Weeping, she gathered up her skirts and ran all the way north. In Pohjola she demanded of Louhi: 'Where is my son?' Louhi said first that she had given him a horse, then that she had sent him hunting. 'You lie!' said the mother. 'Tell the truth, or I will destroy your storehouses and smash your Sampo.' Then Louhi admitted she had sent Lemminkäinen to shoot the swan of Tuonela. The mother searched everywhere. She asked the trees, and the trees said: 'We have troubles enough of our own; we have not seen your son.' She asked the road, and the road said: 'I am trodden and crushed by wheels; I have not seen him.' She asked the moon, and the moon did not know. At last she asked the sun, and the sun said: 'Your son is in the black river of Tuonela, hewn to pieces, lying at the bottom.' The sun, high in the sky, sees everything, and so it alone knew the truth. Hearing it, the mother stopped weeping and turned to find someone who could help her bring her son up from the river.

Evidence / 证据《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第十五章。claim.v0350.kal_2.11
12

铜耙与蜜蜂The copper rake and the bee

母亲哭着去找铁匠伊尔马里宁，请他打一把耙子：铜的耙齿要一百寻长，耙柄要五百寻长。伊尔马里宁为她打好了铜耙。母亲来到图奥内拉的黑河边，请太阳让亡者之地的人们都睡去，然后用铜耙在河里一遍遍地耙，耙出了儿子的衬衫，耙出了他的靴子和帽子，最后在河底耙出了儿子的身体，可还少了一只手、半个头和许多块骨头。她又耙了一遍又一遍，终于把所有的碎块都找齐了。她把碎块拼在一起，请掌管血脉的女神苏奥内塔尔用纺锤把断开的血管一根根接起来，把骨头接上骨头，把肉接上肉。可儿子还是不能说话。母亲就派一只小蜜蜂去取蜜膏，蜜蜂先在草地上采来蜜，没有用；又飞过海去取，还是不够；最后飞过了九重天，从造物主的屋子里取来了神的蜜膏。母亲把蜜膏涂在儿子身上，勒明凯宁醒了过来，说：我睡得多么久啊。母亲问他为什么还想去波赫约拉，他说那个少女还在等他。母亲劝他放弃，带着他回到了家乡。

Weeping, the mother went to the smith Ilmarinen and asked for a rake with copper teeth a hundred fathoms long and a handle five hundred fathoms long, and Ilmarinen forged it. At the black river of Tuonela she asked the sun to put the people of the land of the dead to sleep, then raked the river again and again. She raked up her son's shirt, his boots and his hat, and at last his body from the bottom — but a hand was missing, half the head and many bones. She raked again and again until she had found every piece. She laid the pieces together and called on Suonetar, goddess of the veins, to join the severed veins with her spindle, bone to bone and flesh to flesh. Still her son could not speak. So she sent a little bee for honey. The honey it gathered from the meadows did not help; what it brought from over the sea was not enough; at last it flew beyond the nine heavens and brought the Creator's own honey from his house. The mother anointed her son, and Lemminkäinen woke and said: 'How long I have slept!' When she asked why he still wanted to go to Pohjola, he said the maiden was waiting for him; she persuaded him to give it up and took him home.

Evidence / 证据《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第十五章。claim.v0350.kal_2.12

Editorial boundary / 编辑边界

依据克劳福德 1888 年英译《卡勒瓦拉》第十一至十五章，按诗章顺序讲述。隆洛特在编排勒明凯宁的故事时合并了民间不同英雄的唱本，本篇讲述的是隆洛特的编排；勒明凯宁被砍碎的情节照原诗交代结果，不渲染细节。

芬兰 / Finnish

卡勒瓦拉 · 第三部 库勒沃Kalevala, Part 3: Kullervo

温塔莫与卡勒沃两兄弟因为一连串小事结下深仇，温塔莫杀光了卡勒沃的族人，只留下一个怀孕的女子做奴隶。她生下的库勒沃在摇篮里就发誓复仇。温塔莫三次想杀死他：把他装进桶里扔进湖中，扔进火堆，吊在橡树上，他都活了下来。温塔莫让他干活，他什么都干坏，最后被卖给铁匠伊尔马里宁做奴隶。伊尔马里宁的妻子让他去放牛，在他的面包里烤进一块石头，他父亲留下的唯一遗物——一把刀——在石头上折断了。库勒沃把狼和熊变成牛群赶回家，主妇在挤奶时被它们咬死。他逃进森林，找到了还活着的父母，却在替父亲交税回来的路上诱骗了一个少女，后来才知道她是自己失散多年的妹妹，妹妹投入急流而死。库勒沃出征，灭了温塔莫一族，回到家时亲人都已死去。他来到妹妹遇害的地方，问自己的剑是否愿意饮他的血，然后伏剑而死。

The brothers Untamo and Kalervo fall into a deep feud over a run of petty quarrels; Untamo slays Kalervo's people, sparing only a pregnant woman as a slave. Her son Kullervo vows vengeance in the cradle. Untamo tries three times to kill him — in a barrel thrown into the lake, on a pyre, hanged from an oak — and each time he lives. Every task Kullervo is given he ruins, and at last he is sold as a slave to the smith Ilmarinen. Ilmarinen's wife sends him to herd the cattle and bakes a stone into his bread, on which his father's knife, the only keepsake of his kin, breaks. Kullervo drives home wolves and bears in the shape of cattle, and the mistress is killed as she milks. Fleeing, he finds his parents alive, but on his way home from paying his father's tax he seduces a maiden who proves to be his long-lost sister; she throws herself into the rapids. Kullervo goes to war, destroys Untamo's clan, and comes home to find his family dead. At the place where he wronged his sister he asks his sword whether it will drink his blood, and falls upon it.

01

两兄弟的仇恨The brothers' feud

从前，有一位母亲养大了一窝小鸡，一只被带到了俄罗斯，一只被带到了卡累利阿，还有一只留在家里——诗人用这样的比喻开始讲述两兄弟的故事。哥哥温塔莫和弟弟卡勒沃住得很近，却总是合不来。他们为了渔场、为了田地和羊群，为了一连串鸡毛蒜皮的小事争吵不休，怨恨越积越深。终于，温塔莫召集了一群武士，带着刀剑去攻打卡勒沃。卡勒沃的族人全被杀光，房屋被烧成灰烬，只剩下一个怀了孕的女子活了下来，被温塔莫带回家去，做了打扫屋子、劈柴担水的奴隶。在温塔莫看来，卡勒沃一族已经从世上消失了。可是那个女子腹中的孩子，正是后来让温塔莫一族灭亡的人。在隆洛特编排的《卡勒瓦拉》里，库勒沃的这几章最为阴暗，它们主要取材于卡累利阿和英格里亚一带的民间唱本。二十世纪的作家托尔金也深受这个故事的触动，写下了《库勒沃的故事》。

Once, the poem begins, a mother raised a brood of chicks: one was carried to Russia, one to Karelia, and one stayed at home — with such an image the singer opens the tale of two brothers. The elder, Untamo, and the younger, Kalervo, lived near each other but could never agree. They quarrelled over fishing-grounds, over fields and flocks, over a run of petty matters, and their grudge grew deeper and deeper. At last Untamo gathered a band of warriors and attacked Kalervo with swords. Kalervo's people were all slain and his houses burned to ashes; only one woman, who was with child, survived, and Untamo took her home as a slave to sweep the house, split wood and carry water. To Untamo, Kalervo's line had vanished from the earth. But the child in that woman's womb would one day destroy Untamo's own clan. In Lönnrot's Kalevala these runes are the darkest; they draw chiefly on songs from Karelia and Ingria. In the twentieth century J. R. R. Tolkien was moved by the tale to write his own Story of Kullervo.

Evidence / 证据《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第三十一章。claim.v0350.kal_3.01
02

摇篮里的复仇者The avenger in the cradle

那个女子在温塔莫家里生下了一个男孩，母亲给他取名叫库勒沃，温塔莫的人则叫他“战争之子”。孩子还在摇篮里的时候，就显出了惊人的力气。到了第三个月，他一脚踢开了包着自己的襁褓，把摇篮的底都蹬破了，大家都说：这孩子将来一定会成为一个强壮的人。可是库勒沃一天天长大，心里只有一个念头。有一次，温塔莫听见这个摇篮里的孩子说：等我长大了，有了力气，我要为父亲报仇，为母亲流过的眼泪报仇。温塔莫听了，心里一惊，对家人说：这孩子留着，将来就是我们一族的祸害。他决定趁孩子还小，把他除掉。这个出生在仇人家里的孩子，从一开始就被仇恨包围着。在芬兰语的原诗里，他常被连名带姓地称为“卡勒沃之子库勒沃”，仿佛他的名字本身就背负着父亲一族的命运。这样的话出自一个还在吃奶的孩子之口，温塔莫一家都不寒而栗。

In Untamo's house the woman bore a son. His mother named him Kullervo, and Untamo's people called him the son of war. While still in the cradle he showed astonishing strength: in his third month he kicked off his swaddling clothes and broke the bottom of the cradle, and everyone said he would grow to be a mighty man. But as Kullervo grew, one thought filled his heart. Once Untamo heard the child in the cradle say: 'When I am grown and strong, I will avenge my father and the tears my mother has shed.' Untamo was startled and said to his household: 'If this child lives, he will be the ruin of our clan.' He resolved to be rid of him while he was still small. Born in his enemy's house, the child was surrounded by hatred from the start. In the Finnish poem he is often called by his full name, Kullervo son of Kalervo, as though his very name carried the fate of his father's people. Such words from a child still at the breast chilled Untamo's whole household.

Evidence / 证据《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第三十一章。claim.v0350.kal_3.02
03

杀不死的孩子The child who could not be killed

温塔莫先叫人做了一只木桶，把库勒沃装进去，扔进了湖里。过了三个晚上，人们去看，只见木桶浮在水面上，库勒沃坐在桶上，手里拿着一根铜钓竿，正在钓鱼。温塔莫又叫人砍来一大堆桦木和松木，堆成一座高高的柴堆，把库勒沃扔进火里烧。过了三天，人们去看，只见柴堆已经烧成了灰，库勒沃坐在灰烬里，拿着一根拨火棍，正在拨弄余火，头发一根也没有烧焦。温塔莫又叫人把孩子吊在一棵橡树上。过了三天三夜，人们去看，库勒沃没有死，他坐在树枝上，正在用小刀在树干上刻画，刻的全是手拿刀剑的武士。温塔莫无可奈何，只好说：这孩子杀不死，那就让他做奴隶，替我们干活吧。水、火和绳索都没能杀死他，像是在说这个孩子身上有一种无法消灭的力量；可这股力量后来带给他和身边的人的，却只有灾难。

First Untamo had a barrel made, shut Kullervo inside and threw him into the lake. After three nights his men went to look: the barrel was floating on the water, and Kullervo sat on top of it with a copper rod in his hand, fishing. Next Untamo had a great pile of birch and pine logs heaped up and threw Kullervo into the fire. After three days they went to look: the pile had burned to ashes, and Kullervo sat in the ashes with a poker, stirring the embers, not a hair singed. Then Untamo had the child hanged from an oak. After three days and nights they went to look: Kullervo was not dead but sat on a branch carving pictures on the trunk with a little knife — all of warriors with swords in their hands. Helpless, Untamo said: 'If this child cannot be killed, let him be a slave and work for us.' Water, fire and rope could not kill him, as if the child held a strength nothing could destroy; yet that strength would bring only disaster to him and to those around him.

Evidence / 证据《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第三十一章。claim.v0350.kal_3.03
04

无用的仆人The useless servant

温塔莫给库勒沃派活。先让他照看一个婴儿，他却把婴儿弄伤、弄死了，还把摇篮烧掉；诗中这一段说得很直接，本篇只交代结果。温塔莫又让他去砍林开荒，他把整片森林都砍倒了，然后诅咒那块地永远不长庄稼、不长树木。温塔莫让他筑篱笆，他把整棵整棵的松树和冷杉竖起来，筑起一道高到天上、没有缝隙也没有门的围墙，谁也进不去出不来。温塔莫让他打黑麦，他把黑麦打成了粉末和糠皮。温塔莫说：这个孩子什么活都干不好，留着他只会带来灾祸。他就把库勒沃卖到了卡累利阿，卖给了铁匠伊尔马里宁，作价不过是几口旧锅和一些破旧的农具。库勒沃就这样从仇人的奴隶，变成了陌生人家的奴隶。库勒沃并不是懒惰，他力大无穷，只是心里装满了怨恨，每一件活计到了他手里，都变成了破坏。伊尔马里宁并不知道，自己买回家的是怎样一个人。

Untamo set Kullervo to work. First he was told to mind a baby; he hurt it and it died, and he burned the cradle — the poem tells it bluntly, and this retelling gives only the outcome. Next he was sent to clear the forest; he felled the whole forest and cursed the land so that neither grain nor tree would ever grow there. Told to build a fence, he set up whole pines and firs into a wall reaching the sky, with no gap and no gate, so that no one could get in or out. Told to thresh the rye, he beat it to dust and chaff. Untamo said: 'This boy can do nothing right; keeping him will only bring misfortune.' So he sold Kullervo into Karelia, to the smith Ilmarinen, for no more than a few worn-out kettles and some battered farm tools. So Kullervo passed from slave in his enemy's house to slave in a stranger's. Kullervo was not idle; he was enormously strong, but so full of resentment that every task in his hands turned to destruction. Ilmarinen did not know what kind of man he had brought home.

Evidence / 证据《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第三十一章。claim.v0350.kal_3.04
05

藏着石头的面包The bread with a stone in it

伊尔马里宁的妻子，就是当年那位波赫约拉的少女，如今是铁匠家的女主人。她看着这个新来的奴隶，心里想：让他去放牛吧。她要给库勒沃准备路上吃的干粮，就烤了一块面包：上面是燕麦，下面是小麦，中间却藏了一块石头。她把面包交给库勒沃，叮嘱他：等牛群进了树林，你再吃这块面包。然后，她向乌戈、森林的主人和森林之母念了很长的祈祷，请他们保佑牛群平安，不受狼和熊的伤害，又念起对熊的咒语，请熊不要伤害她的牛。库勒沃赶着牛群出了门，在沼泽和林间放牧，一路上抱怨自己的命运：别人吃的是白面包，喝的是麦酒，而他这个奴隶，只能吃干硬的面包，在荒野里放牛。原诗里，她的祈祷占了这一章的大半篇幅，保存了古代芬兰牧人祈求牲畜平安、驱赶猛兽的咒语。读者也就更明白，后面她的牛群为什么会在狼和熊的手里遭殃。

Ilmarinen's wife — the maiden of Pohjola of old, now mistress of the smith's house — looked at the new slave and thought: let him herd the cattle. To provide for him she baked a loaf: oats on top, wheat below, and in the middle a stone. She gave it to Kullervo and told him not to eat it until the herd had gone into the woods. Then she spoke long prayers to Ukko and to the master and mother of the forest, asking them to keep the herd safe from wolf and bear, and chanted the charms to the bear, begging it to spare her cattle. Kullervo drove the herd out and pastured them through swamp and wood, lamenting his lot as he went: others ate white bread and drank ale, while he, a slave, had only hard bread and the cattle in the wilderness. In the poem her prayers fill most of the rune, preserving the charms with which old Finnish herders asked safety for their cattle and kept off wild beasts — which makes plain why her herd later comes to grief by wolf and bear.

Evidence / 证据《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第三十二章。claim.v0350.kal_3.05
06

断刀The broken knife

到了中午，库勒沃坐在山坡上，拿出主妇给的面包，用刀一切，刀刃碰到了中间的石头，啪的一声折断了。这把刀是他父亲留下的唯一遗物，是他与被杀光的卡勒沃一族之间仅剩的联系。库勒沃看着断刀，哭了起来，说：这是我唯一的珍宝，是我父亲的刀，如今竟断在一个女主人的石头上。一只乌鸦从树上对他说：你这卡勒沃的孩子，为什么这样悲伤？把牛群赶进沼泽吧，让狼和熊把它们都吃掉，再把狼和熊召来，让它们变成牛的样子，傍晚赶回家去。库勒沃照着乌鸦的话做了：他把牛群赶进沼泽，让狼和熊吃掉了它们，又用咒语把狼变成了牛，把熊变成了母牛，赶着这群野兽，一路吹着号角，向主人家走去。这一刀断下去，断的不只是一把刀，也是库勒沃心中最后的一点忍耐。他把断刀收好，心里只想着怎样报复那个女主人。

At noon Kullervo sat down on a hillside, took out the mistress's loaf and cut into it; the blade struck the stone in the middle and snapped. The knife was the only keepsake left by his father, his last link with the slaughtered people of Kalervo. Kullervo looked at the broken knife and wept: 'This was my only treasure, my father's knife, and it has broken on a mistress's stone.' A crow called to him from a tree: 'Child of Kalervo, why so sad? Drive the herd into the swamp and let the wolves and bears devour them; then call the wolves and bears, give them the shape of cattle, and drive them home at evening.' Kullervo did as the crow said: he drove the herd into the swamp to be devoured, then by his charms turned the wolves into oxen and the bears into cows, and drove the beasts towards his master's house, blowing his horn. With the blade broke the last of Kullervo's patience. He put the broken knife away, thinking only of how to repay the mistress.

Evidence / 证据《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第三十三章。claim.v0350.kal_3.06
07

主妇之死The death of the mistress

傍晚，库勒沃把那群“牛”赶进了牛栏，号角声响彻四方。伊尔马里宁的妻子高兴地说：感谢乌戈，牛群平安回来了。她提着奶桶去挤奶，俯下身去，那头“母牛”却原来是一只熊，扑上来把她撕咬。她惊叫着向库勒沃求救：好心的牧人啊，救救我，拿开这些野兽吧，我会给你最好的衣服，最好的面包。库勒沃说：你给我吃石头做的面包，现在你自己尝尝苦头吧。她又向乌戈祈求，请他用箭射死库勒沃。可是没有人来救她，伊尔马里宁的妻子就这样死在了牛栏里。这位曾经在彩虹上织布、让万奈莫宁和伊尔马里宁都为之倾倒的少女，就因为一块藏在面包里的石头，丢掉了性命。库勒沃吹起号角，离开了铁匠的家，逃进了森林。伊尔马里宁后来失去了妻子，悲伤不已。他为她哭了许多日夜；后面的诗章会讲到，他甚至想用金子和银子为自己打造一个新的妻子。

At evening Kullervo drove his 'cattle' into the byre, the horn sounding far and wide. Ilmarinen's wife said joyfully: 'Thanks be to Ukko, the herd has come home safe.' She took her milking pail and bent to milk, but the 'cow' was a bear, which sprang on her and tore her. She shrieked to Kullervo for help: 'Good herdsman, save me, drive off these beasts, and I will give you the best clothes and the best bread.' Kullervo answered: 'You fed me bread made of stone; now taste your own bitterness.' She prayed to Ukko to shoot Kullervo with his arrows. But no one came to save her, and Ilmarinen's wife died in the byre. The maiden who once wove on the rainbow, for whom Väinämöinen and Ilmarinen had both longed, lost her life over a stone hidden in a loaf. Kullervo blew his horn, left the smith's house and fled into the forest. Ilmarinen was left to grieve for his wife. He wept for her many nights; a later rune tells how he even tried to forge himself a new wife of gold and silver.

Evidence / 证据《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第三十三章。claim.v0350.kal_3.07
08

找到父母Finding his parents

库勒沃在森林里游荡，心中充满了悲伤和愤怒。他想：我该到哪里去？我是谁的孩子？我从来没有一个家。他决定去找温塔莫报仇。在林中，他遇见一个穿着蓝衣的老妇人，她对他说：卡勒沃的孩子，你的父亲并没有死，他还活着，你的母亲也活着，他们就住在拉普兰的边上，靠近一片湖。库勒沃半信半疑地出发了，走了很久，终于在湖边找到了一座房子，见到了自己的父亲和母亲。母亲哭着说：我的儿子，我以为你早就死了，还为你流了许多眼泪。我还以为你是被卖到远方去了。他们告诉他，他还有一个姐姐，可是很多年前，她到林子里去采浆果，就再也没有回来，谁也不知道她去了哪里。这是库勒沃一生中少有的温暖时刻：他终于有了一个家，有了父亲和母亲。可那个失踪的姐姐，却像一道阴影，留在了故事里。

Kullervo wandered in the forest, full of grief and anger. 'Where shall I go? Whose child am I? I have never had a home.' He resolved to go and take vengeance on Untamo. In the woods he met an old woman in a blue robe, who said: 'Child of Kalervo, your father is not dead. He lives, and your mother lives too; they dwell on the borders of Lapland, near a lake.' Half believing, Kullervo set out, and after long wandering found a house by a lake and saw his father and mother. His mother wept: 'My son, I thought you long dead and shed many tears for you; I thought you had been sold far away.' They told him that he had an elder sister, but that years ago she had gone into the woods to pick berries and never come back, and no one knew where she had gone. It is one of the few warm moments of Kullervo's life: at last he had a home, a father and a mother. But the lost sister lingers in the story like a shadow.

Evidence / 证据《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第三十四章。claim.v0350.kal_3.08
09

路上的少女The maiden on the road

回到家里，库勒沃想帮父母干活，却什么也干不好：父亲让他划船，他把船桨划断了，把船底都划穿了；让他撒网捕鱼，他把水搅成了泥浆，把渔网撕成了碎片。父亲只好派他去交税。库勒沃交完了税，赶着雪橇回家，在路上遇见一个少女，请她坐上自己的雪橇，她不肯；又遇见一个少女，也不肯。第三次，他遇见一个在荒野里赶路的少女，就用银子和漂亮的布料引诱她，把她拉上了雪橇。两人在雪橇上过了一夜。第二天早晨，少女问他是哪一家的人。库勒沃说：我是卡勒沃的儿子。少女听了，脸色大变，说：我也是卡勒沃的女儿，就是多年前在林子里采浆果时迷了路的那个女儿。他们谁也不知道对方是谁，两个失散多年的孩子，就在这样的误会里相遇了。这一夜，成了两个人一生中最大的不幸。

Back home, Kullervo tried to help his parents but could do nothing right. Set to row, he broke the oars and drove the boat's bottom through; set to fish, he churned the water to mud and tore the net to shreds. So his father sent him to pay the taxes. Driving home in his sledge after paying them, he met a maiden on the road and asked her into his sledge; she refused. He met another, who also refused. The third time he met a maiden travelling across the wilds, and with silver and fine cloth he lured her and drew her into the sledge. They spent the night together. In the morning the maiden asked him what family he came from. Kullervo said: 'I am the son of Kalervo.' At this her face changed, and she said: 'I too am Kalervo's daughter — the daughter who lost her way picking berries in the woods long ago.' Neither knew who the other was; two children lost for years met in this terrible ignorance. That night became the greatest misfortune of both their lives.

Evidence / 证据《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第三十五章。claim.v0350.kal_3.09
10

急流The rapids

少女明白了一切，悲痛欲绝。她从雪橇上跳下来，奔向河边那奔腾的急流，说：我宁愿让急流把我卷走，也不愿再活在这世上。她投身于激流之中，被汹涌的河水吞没了。库勒沃站在河边，悔恨交加，他说：我做了什么样的事啊！我毁了我的妹妹，我毁了我自己，我这一生只给别人带来不幸。他一度想就此结束自己的生命。他回到家里，把这件事告诉了母亲。母亲劝他说：不要死，我的儿子，你可以远远地走开，到一个没有人认识你的地方去，等时间慢慢平息你的悲伤。可是库勒沃说：在我死之前，还有一件事要做。我要去找温塔莫，为我父亲的族人报仇。诗中说她在投水之前留下了悲伤的话，哀叹自己生来就不幸。库勒沃的一生，从仇人家的摇篮开始，到这里，已经只剩下了复仇和悔恨。

The maiden understood everything and was overcome with grief. She leapt from the sledge and ran to the roaring rapids of the river, crying that she would rather be swept away by the torrent than live on in the world. She threw herself into the rapids and was swallowed by the raging waters. Kullervo stood by the river, torn with remorse: 'What have I done! I have ruined my sister and ruined myself; all my life I have brought only misfortune on others.' For a while he thought of ending his own life. He went home and told his mother. She pleaded: 'Do not die, my son. Go far away, to a place where no one knows you, and let time ease your grief.' But Kullervo said: 'Before I die there is one thing left to do. I will go to Untamo and avenge my father's people.' The poem gives her sorrowful words before she leaps, lamenting that she was born to misfortune. Kullervo's life, begun in an enemy's cradle, now held nothing but vengeance and remorse.

Evidence / 证据《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第三十五章。claim.v0350.kal_3.10
11

出征与复仇War and vengeance

库勒沃准备出征，他一个个地问家人：我死了，你们会为我哭泣吗？父亲说：不会，我会再生一个比你更好的儿子。哥哥说：不会，我会找一个比你更好的兄弟。姐妹说：不会，我会找一个比你更好的兄弟。只有母亲说：我会为你哭泣，我会在屋里哭，在田里哭，在每一个地方哭，哭到我的眼泪流干。库勒沃上了路。打仗的途中，一个个使者跑来告诉他：你的父亲死了，你的哥哥死了，你的姐妹死了。他都不肯回去，只说：让他们安葬吧。最后使者说：你的母亲死了。他才流下了眼泪。他向乌戈祈求一把好剑，乌戈给了他。库勒沃来到温塔莫的家，把温塔莫的族人全部杀死，烧毁了他们的房屋，只留下一片灰烬和石头。父亲的仇，终于报了。全家人里，只有母亲的爱从未改变。可是对库勒沃来说，复仇并没有带来安慰，回家时迎接他的只有冷清。

As he made ready for war, Kullervo asked each of his family: 'When I die, will you weep for me?' His father said: 'No; I will beget a better son.' His brother said: 'No; I will find a better brother.' His sister said: 'No; I will find a better brother.' Only his mother said: 'I will weep for you, in the house and in the fields and everywhere, until my tears run dry.' Kullervo set out. On the way messengers came one after another: your father is dead, your brother is dead, your sister is dead. He would not turn back, saying only: let them be buried. At last a messenger said: your mother is dead. Then he wept. He prayed to Ukko for a good sword, and Ukko gave it. Coming to Untamo's house, Kullervo slew all of Untamo's people and burned their dwellings, leaving only ashes and stones. His father's death was avenged at last. Of all his family, only his mother's love had never changed. Yet vengeance brought Kullervo no comfort; only emptiness awaited him at home.

Evidence / 证据《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第三十六章。claim.v0350.kal_3.11
12

卡勒沃之子的结局The end of Kalervo's son

库勒沃回到家里，家中空无一人，炉灶冰冷，父亲、母亲、兄弟和姐妹都已经死去。他在母亲的坟前哭泣，母亲在坟墓里对他说：带上我们的黑狗穆斯蒂，到森林里去吧，向森林的神灵求一个安身的地方。库勒沃带着狗走进森林，不知不觉来到了当年他诱骗妹妹的那片荒野。那里的草不再生长，树叶凋零，仿佛大地也在为那件事哀悼。库勒沃拔出剑来，问它：我的剑啊，你愿意饮一个有罪之人的血吗？剑回答说：我连无辜者的血都饮过，为什么不能饮你这有罪之人的血？库勒沃把剑柄插在地上，剑尖朝上，扑倒在剑上死去了。诗的最后，老万奈莫宁听说了这一切，说：以后的人们啊，不要用错误的方式抚养孩子，不要让孩子在陌生人的摇篮里长大，否则他永远学不会正直。卡勒沃之子库勒沃的故事，就这样结束了。

Kullervo came home to find the house empty and the hearth cold; father, mother, brother and sister were all dead. He wept at his mother's grave, and from the grave his mother said: 'Take our black dog Musti and go into the forest, and ask the spirits of the forest for a place to rest.' Kullervo went into the forest with the dog and came, without knowing it, to the very wilds where he had wronged his sister. The grass there no longer grew and the leaves had withered, as if the earth itself mourned what had happened. Kullervo drew his sword and asked it: 'My sword, will you drink the blood of a guilty man?' The sword answered: 'I have drunk the blood of the innocent; why should I not drink yours, who are guilty?' Kullervo set the hilt in the ground, point upward, and fell upon it and died. At the end of the rune old Väinämöinen hears of it all and says: people of the future, never raise a child wrongly, never let him grow up in a stranger's cradle, or he will never learn to be upright. So ended the story of Kullervo, son of Kalervo.

Evidence / 证据《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第三十六章。claim.v0350.kal_3.12

Editorial boundary / 编辑边界

依据克劳福德 1888 年英译《卡勒瓦拉》第三十一至三十六章，按诗章顺序讲述。库勒沃的故事涉及屠杀、虐待、兄妹乱伦与自杀，本篇照原诗交代结果，不渲染细节；温塔莫与卡勒沃结仇的具体缘由与卖身的作价只概括讲述。

芬兰 / Finnish

卡勒瓦拉 · 第四部 夺取三宝Kalevala, Part 4: the theft of the Sampo

万奈莫宁、伊尔马里宁和勒明凯宁乘着一艘渴望出征的战船前往北方，去夺回为波赫约拉锻造的三宝。船在急流中卡在一条巨大的梭鱼背上，万奈莫宁杀死梭鱼，用它的颚骨做成了第一把康特勒琴。他的琴声让天上地下所有的生灵都来倾听，连他自己也流下了眼泪，泪水落进海里，变成了蓝色的珍珠。到了波赫约拉，洛希不肯分享三宝，万奈莫宁就用琴声把整个北方唱入梦乡。英雄们打开铜山的门锁，用牛犁断三宝的根，把它搬上船逃走。勒明凯宁忍不住在船上唱歌，一只鹤被惊醒，叫醒了波赫约拉。洛希派来浓雾、海怪和风暴，康特勒琴落进了大海；最后她化作一只巨鹰，带着上百名武士扑向战船。万奈莫宁用船舵打断了她的爪子，三宝跌进海里摔得粉碎：大块沉入海底，成了大海的财富，小块漂到卡勒瓦拉的岸边，带来了丰收；洛希只抢回了三宝的盖子，波赫约拉从此贫穷下去。

Väinämöinen, Ilmarinen and Lemminkäinen sail north in a war-boat that longs for battle, to win back the Sampo forged for Pohjola. In the rapids the boat sticks on the back of a giant pike; Väinämöinen kills it and from its jawbone makes the first kantele, whose music draws every creature of earth and sky to listen; he weeps himself, and his tears fall into the sea as blue pearls. In Pohjola Louhi will not share the Sampo, so Väinämöinen plays all the north to sleep; the heroes open the copper mountain, plough out the Sampo's roots with an ox, and carry it off in their boat. Lemminkäinen cannot help singing, a crane wakes and rouses Pohjola, and Louhi sends fog, a sea monster and a storm that sweeps the kantele overboard; at last she becomes a giant eagle carrying a hundred warriors. Väinämöinen smashes her talons with the rudder; the Sampo falls into the sea and shatters: the large pieces become the riches of the sea, the small ones drift to the shores of Kalevala and bring plenty, and Louhi takes home only the lid, so that Pohjola grows poor.

01

宝剑与哭泣的船The sword and the weeping boat

伊尔马里宁失去了妻子，悲伤了很久。万奈莫宁对他说：我们到北方的波赫约拉去吧，去把三宝夺回来。你为他们锻造了三宝，他们却只给我们带来不幸；三宝在那里磨出粮食、磨出财富，让北方富足，我们却一无所有。伊尔马里宁说：三宝锁在波赫约拉的石山里，有九道锁，根扎进地下九寻深，很难拿到。可他还是答应了，并且为万奈莫宁打造了一把宝剑：剑刃上有月亮和太阳，剑柄上有星星，剑身上有一匹马在嘶鸣，剑柄的圆头上有一只猫在叫，剑鞘上有一只狗在吠。两位英雄骑马出发，走到海边，听见岸边有一艘船在哭泣。那是一艘战船，它哭着说：别的船都去打仗，带回金银财宝，只有我被丢在这里，在木屑堆里一年年地腐烂。万奈莫宁说：不要哭，我会带你去打仗的。他唱起歌来，船自己滑进了水里，两位英雄登上船，向北方驶去。

Ilmarinen grieved long for his lost wife. Väinämöinen said to him: 'Let us go north to Pohjola and win back the Sampo. You forged it for them, yet they bring us only misfortune; there it grinds grain and wealth and makes the north rich, while we have nothing.' Ilmarinen said: 'The Sampo is locked in the stone mountain of Pohjola behind nine locks, its roots nine fathoms deep; it will be hard to take.' But he agreed, and forged Väinämöinen a sword: on its blade the moon and the sun, on its hilt the stars, on its side a horse neighing, on the knob of the hilt a cat mewing, on the scabbard a dog barking. The two heroes rode to the sea and heard a boat weeping on the shore. It was a war-boat, and it wept: 'The other boats go to war and bring home gold and silver; only I am left here, rotting year after year among the wood-chips.' 'Do not weep,' said Väinämöinen, 'I will take you to war.' He sang, the boat slid into the water of itself, and the heroes boarded it and sailed north.

Evidence / 证据《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第三十九章。claim.v0350.kal_4.01
02

勒明凯宁加入Lemminkäinen joins them

船经过一座岬角时，岸上有人在喊：是谁在海上航行？原来是勒明凯宁。他一个人住在海边，正因为没有了打仗的机会而闷闷不乐，看见两位英雄的船驶过，就大声问他们要到哪里去。万奈莫宁说：我们要到北方的波赫约拉去，去夺回三宝。勒明凯宁说：让我也一起去吧，我会是第三个英雄，我的剑也很锋利，我能在打仗的时候帮上你们的忙。万奈莫宁答应了。勒明凯宁拿着一块木板跳上了船，船身沉了一沉，又平稳地向前驶去。万奈莫宁坐在船尾掌舵，伊尔马里宁和勒明凯宁划桨，船儿像飞鸟一样在海浪上前进。三位卡勒瓦拉最有名的英雄——歌者、铁匠和战士——第一次一同出发，去完成一件谁也没有做到过的事。这位战士在前面的诗章里曾在波赫约拉闯下大祸，不得不逃到海岛上躲了三年，如今他又一次站到了冒险的船上。

As the boat passed a headland, someone on the shore called out: 'Who is sailing on the sea?' It was Lemminkäinen. Living alone by the sea and sullen for lack of a war to fight, he saw the heroes' boat go by and shouted to ask where they were going. Väinämöinen said: 'We are going north to Pohjola, to win back the Sampo.' Lemminkäinen said: 'Let me come too. I will be the third hero; my sword is sharp too, and I can help you in the fighting.' Väinämöinen agreed. Lemminkäinen leapt aboard with a board under his arm; the boat dipped and then sailed steadily on. Väinämöinen sat at the stern steering, Ilmarinen and Lemminkäinen rowed, and the boat sped over the waves like a bird. The three most famous heroes of Kalevala — the singer, the smith and the warrior — set out together for the first time, to do what no one had ever done. In earlier runes this warrior had brought disaster on himself in Pohjola and had to hide on an island for three years; now he stood once more aboard a boat bound for adventure.

Evidence / 证据《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第三十九章。claim.v0350.kal_4.02
03

大梭鱼The great pike

船驶进一段湍急的河道，在急流和瀑布之间穿行。万奈莫宁念着咒语，请急流的女神和水中的精灵让船平安通过。可就在急流中央，船忽然停住了，任凭怎么划桨也纹丝不动，好像被什么东西紧紧托住。勒明凯宁探身往水里一看，说：船下面不是礁石，也不是树干，而是一条巨大的梭鱼，我们的船正卡在它的背上。他拔剑向水里砍去，可是用力太猛，自己差点掉进河里，剑也没能伤到梭鱼。伊尔马里宁抓住他的头发，把他拉了回来。伊尔马里宁也拔剑去砍，剑却折断了，梭鱼仍然一动不动。最后，万奈莫宁拔出自己的宝剑，猛地刺进水里，从梭鱼的身下一挑，把这条巨大的鱼刺穿，挑出水面，劈成了几段。他们把梭鱼拖上船，在岸边煮熟，三位英雄美美地吃了一顿，只剩下一堆鱼骨。

The boat ran into a stretch of wild river, threading between rapids and falls. Väinämöinen chanted charms to the goddess of the rapids and the spirits of the water to let them pass safely. But in the middle of the rapids the boat suddenly stopped, and however they rowed it would not move, as if something held it fast. Lemminkäinen leaned over and looked: 'It is no rock and no tree-trunk beneath us, but a giant pike; our boat is stuck on its back.' He drew his sword and struck into the water, but struck so hard that he nearly fell in, and did the pike no harm; Ilmarinen caught him by the hair and pulled him back. Ilmarinen struck too, and his sword broke, and the pike did not stir. At last Väinämöinen drew his own sword, thrust it into the water and up under the fish, pierced the great pike, lifted it out and cut it in pieces. They hauled it aboard, cooked it on the shore, and the three heroes ate their fill, leaving only a heap of bones.

Evidence / 证据《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第四十章。claim.v0350.kal_4.03
04

第一把康特勒琴The first kantele

万奈莫宁看着那堆鱼骨，心想：这些骨头要是做成一件东西，会是什么样子？他拿起梭鱼的颚骨，说：如果有一位巧手的工匠，就能用它做成一件乐器。可是谁也不会做，万奈莫宁就自己动手。他用梭鱼的颚骨做成琴身，用梭鱼的牙齿做成调弦的琴钉，又从恶灵希西那匹骟马的身上取来马鬃，做成了琴弦。这样，世界上第一把康特勒琴就造成了。伊尔马里宁和勒明凯宁都想试一试，他们拨动琴弦，发出的却是刺耳难听的声音。他们把琴带到波赫约拉，那里的人们也争着去弹，有年轻人，有老人，有少女，可没有一个人能弹出好听的曲子，琴声粗哑，人们捂着耳朵，说这琴毫无用处，还是扔进水里算了。可是琴自己哭了起来，说它不愿被扔进水里，它只等着一位真正懂得它的人来弹奏。

Looking at the heap of bones, Väinämöinen wondered what they might become. He took up the pike's jawbone and said: 'A skilled craftsman could make an instrument of this.' No one knew how, so he set to it himself. From the jawbone he made the body of the harp, from the pike's teeth the pegs, and for strings he took hair from the gelding of the evil spirit Hiisi. So the first kantele in the world was made. Ilmarinen and Lemminkäinen both tried it, but when they plucked the strings the sound was harsh and ugly. In Pohjola people crowded to play it — young men and old, maidens too — but no one could draw a fair tune from it; the sound was rough, people covered their ears, and said the harp was useless and had better be thrown into the water. But the kantele wept, saying it would not be thrown away; it was waiting for one who truly understood it.

Evidence / 证据《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第四十章。claim.v0350.kal_4.04
05

万物倾听All creatures listen

万奈莫宁洗净双手，坐在一块歌唱的石头上，把康特勒琴放在膝上，用手指拨动琴弦。第一声响起，四周就安静了下来；琴声越来越美，传遍了山林和湖海。森林里的松鼠从这根树枝跳到那根树枝，跑来倾听；白鼬、麋鹿、山猫都来了，狼从沼泽里走出来，熊爬上了篱笆。森林之王塔皮奥和他的家人穿着盛装来到山岗上。天上的鸟儿也飞来了：鹰离开了巢，鹞子从高空落下，天鹅从湖上飞来，就连小小的燕雀也聚在他的肩头。水里的鱼儿都游到岸边，梭鱼、鲑鱼和白鲑把头伸出水面。海王阿赫托也从海底升起，坐在一朵睡莲上倾听。天上的少女们——月亮的女儿和太阳的女儿——正在纺金线、织银布，听见琴声，手里的纺锤都掉了下来。万奈莫宁一连弹了许多天，所有的生灵都被琴声迷住了。

Väinämöinen washed his hands, sat down on a stone of singing, set the kantele on his knee and plucked the strings with his fingers. At the first note all around fell silent; the music grew ever lovelier and spread through hills, woods, lakes and seas. The squirrels of the forest leapt from branch to branch to listen; ermine, elk and lynx came, the wolf came out of the swamp and the bear climbed onto the fence. Tapio, king of the forest, came with his household in festive dress to the hilltop. The birds of the sky came too: the eagle left its nest, the hawk dropped from the heights, the swans flew in from the lakes, and even the little finches gathered on his shoulders. The fishes swam to the shore, pike, salmon and whitefish lifting their heads from the water. Ahto, king of the sea, rose from the depths and sat on a water-lily to listen. The maidens of the sky — the daughters of the moon and of the sun, spinning golden thread and weaving silver cloth — let their spindles fall at the sound. Väinämöinen played for many days, and every creature was enchanted.

Evidence / 证据《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第四十一章。claim.v0350.kal_4.05
06

泪珠The tears that became pearls

所有听见琴声的人都哭了：年轻的人哭了，老人哭了，男人和女人都哭了，连小孩子也哭了。最后，万奈莫宁自己也被琴声打动，流下了眼泪。他的泪珠比越橘还大，比豌豆还圆，比鸡蛋还要光亮，一颗颗从他的眼里落下，落到脸颊上，从脸颊落到胸前，从胸前落到膝上，从膝上落到脚下，又从脚下滚进了大海，沉到了海底的黑泥里。万奈莫宁说：谁能把我的眼泪从海底捞上来？乌鸦来试，没有成功。一只蓝色的野鸭飞来，潜进海里，把那些泪珠一颗颗衔了上来。泪珠已经变了样：它们变成了蓝色的珍珠，美丽得可以戴在国王的头上，成为英雄们永远的装饰。这是《卡勒瓦拉》里最安静的时刻之一：在夺取三宝的长途中，歌者停下来，让音乐和眼泪说话。那只野鸭，在原诗里是一只蓝色的鸭子。

Everyone who heard the music wept: the young and the old, men and women, even the little children. At last Väinämöinen himself was moved by his playing and began to weep. His tears were larger than cranberries, rounder than peas, brighter than eggs; they fell from his eyes onto his cheeks, from his cheeks onto his breast, from his breast to his knees, from his knees to his feet, and from his feet rolled into the sea and sank into the dark mud of the bottom. 'Who will bring my tears up from the sea?' said Väinämöinen. The raven tried and failed. A blue duck came, dived into the sea and brought the tears up one by one. They had changed: they had become blue pearls, beautiful enough to crown a king, an ornament for heroes for ever. It is one of the quietest moments in the Kalevala: on the long road to the Sampo the singer pauses, and lets music and tears speak. In the poem the duck is a blue duck.

Evidence / 证据《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第四十一章。claim.v0350.kal_4.06
07

唱睡波赫约拉Singing Pohjola to sleep

船终于到了波赫约拉。英雄们走进洛希的大厅，洛希问他们来做什么。万奈莫宁说：我们来商量三宝的事。三宝在你们这里磨出了粮食和财富，我们也想分享一份。如果你不肯分给我们，我们就把它整个拿走。洛希说：一只松鼠不能分给三个人，一个三宝也不能分给两家。三宝留在波赫约拉，在这里转动，在这里磨面。万奈莫宁说：既然如此，我们就把它全部带回卡勒瓦拉。洛希大怒，召集了波赫约拉的全部武士，手持刀剑围了上来。万奈莫宁不慌不忙，拿起康特勒琴弹奏起来。琴声一响，波赫约拉的人们都停下了脚步，一个个闭上眼睛，倒在地上沉沉睡去。万奈莫宁又从口袋里掏出“睡眠之针”，把他们的睫毛缝在一起，让他们久久不能醒来。整个北方都陷入了沉睡。在这部史诗里，琴声和歌声比刀剑更有力量。

At last the boat reached Pohjola. The heroes went into Louhi's hall, and she asked their business. Väinämöinen said: 'We have come to speak of the Sampo. Here it grinds grain and wealth for you; we want a share. If you will not share it, we will take the whole.' Louhi said: 'A squirrel cannot be shared among three, and one Sampo cannot be shared between two households. The Sampo stays in Pohjola, to turn here and grind here.' 'Then we will take it all to Kalevala,' said Väinämöinen. Furious, Louhi summoned all the warriors of Pohjola, who closed in with swords. Unhurried, Väinämöinen took up his kantele and played. At the first notes the people of Pohjola stood still, closed their eyes one by one, and fell to the ground in deep sleep. Then he took his needles of sleep from his pouch and stitched their eyelashes together so that they would not wake for a long time. All the north lay asleep. In this epic the harp and the song are mightier than the sword.

Evidence / 证据《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第四十二章。claim.v0350.kal_4.07
08

挖出三宝Digging out the Sampo

英雄们来到波赫约拉的铜山前，三宝就锁在山里的九道门后。万奈莫宁轻声唱起开锁的歌，门锁一道道松开了；伊尔马里宁在门轴上抹了黄油，让沉重的铜门打开时不会发出吱呀的响声，免得惊醒睡着的人们。门开了，三宝就在里面，它的根深深地扎进了山岩和地下。勒明凯宁说：让我来，我力气最大。他用脚抵着地，双手抱住三宝，用尽全力往上拔，三宝却纹丝不动，它的根扎得太深了。于是他们牵来波赫约拉最大的一头公牛，套上犁，用犁把三宝的根一根根犁断。三宝终于松动了，英雄们把它从山里抬出来，搬上了船，藏在船舱里。他们解开缆绳，悄悄地离开了波赫约拉的海岸，划着船，向南方的家乡驶去。原诗在第十章里说过，三宝的根有三条：一条扎进大地，一条扎进水边，一条扎进家门前的山丘；如今这三条根都被犁断了，三宝离开了它扎根多年的地方。

The heroes came to the copper mountain of Pohjola, where the Sampo was locked behind nine doors. Väinämöinen softly sang the song that opens locks, and the locks loosened one by one; Ilmarinen smeared butter on the hinges so that the heavy copper doors would open without creaking and wake the sleepers. The doors opened, and there was the Sampo, its roots sunk deep in the rock and the earth. 'Let me,' said Lemminkäinen, 'I am strongest.' He braced his feet, clasped the Sampo in his arms and heaved with all his strength, but it did not move; its roots went too deep. So they brought the greatest ox of Pohjola, yoked it to a plough, and ploughed through the Sampo's roots one by one. At last the Sampo came loose; the heroes carried it out of the mountain, loaded it into the boat and hid it in the hold. They cast off and slipped quietly away from the shores of Pohjola, rowing south towards home. Rune X had told of the Sampo's three roots, one in the earth, one at the water's edge, one in the hill by the house; now all three were ploughed through, and the Sampo left the place where it had been rooted so long.

Evidence / 证据《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第四十二章。claim.v0350.kal_4.08
09

鹤的叫声The crane's cry

船在海上平稳地航行，三宝藏在船舱里，三位英雄心里都很高兴。勒明凯宁按捺不住，说：我们夺得了三宝，这样的喜事，怎么能不唱歌呢？万奈莫宁劝他说：现在还不是唱歌的时候。唱歌会被人听见，会把波赫约拉的人吵醒，等我们回到家乡再唱吧。勒明凯宁忍了一天、两天，到了第三天，他再也忍不住了，张开嘴就唱了起来。可他的嗓子粗哑难听，歌声在海面上远远传开。一只鹤正站在沼泽边的草丛里，被这难听的歌声吓了一跳，扑腾着翅膀飞了起来，一路尖叫着飞向北方。它的叫声越过了山岭和海湾，飞进了波赫约拉，把那些被缝住睫毛、沉睡已久的人们全都吵醒了。洛希醒来，跑到铜山一看，三宝不见了。一次不合时宜的歌唱，就这样毁掉了万奈莫宁小心翼翼的计划，追兵很快就要来了。

The boat sailed smoothly over the sea with the Sampo hidden in the hold, and the three heroes were glad. Lemminkäinen could not contain himself: 'We have won the Sampo — how can we not sing at such joy?' Väinämöinen warned him: 'This is no time for singing. Song will be heard and will wake the people of Pohjola. Wait until we are home.' Lemminkäinen held back one day, two days, but on the third he could hold back no longer and began to sing. His voice was harsh and ugly, and the song carried far over the water. A crane standing in the reeds by a swamp was startled by the dreadful singing, flapped up, and flew screaming north. Its cry crossed hills and bays and reached Pohjola, waking all the people who had slept so long with their eyelashes sewn. Louhi woke, ran to the copper mountain, and found the Sampo gone. One song at the wrong moment undid all Väinämöinen's careful plans, and the pursuit would soon be upon them.

Evidence / 证据《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第四十二章。claim.v0350.kal_4.09
10

雾、海怪与风暴Fog, the sea monster and the storm

洛希大怒，施展魔法追赶英雄们。她先派来浓雾的少女，让大雾笼罩了海面，英雄们的船在雾中迷失了方向，一连三天三夜停在原地。万奈莫宁拔出宝剑，向大雾劈去，劈开了一条路，雾气四散，船又能前进了。接着，洛希唤起了海怪伊库-图尔索。海怪从海底升起，掀起巨浪，要把船掀翻。万奈莫宁伸手抓住海怪的耳朵，把它提出水面，问它：伊库-图尔索，你为什么从海里升起来，挡在我们的路上？他命令海怪沉回海底，永远不许再在人们面前出现。海怪沉了下去。最后，洛希向乌戈求来一场狂风暴雨，海浪滔天，船身摇晃，万奈莫宁心爱的康特勒琴被一阵大浪卷下船去，沉进了海底。万奈莫宁看着大海，伤心地说：我的快乐已经沉进了海里，再也找不回来了。这把琴后来再也没有找回来，万奈莫宁不得不在后面的诗章里重新做了一把。

Louhi in her fury worked magic to pursue the heroes. First she sent the maiden of the mist, and a thick fog covered the sea; the heroes' boat lost its way and lay still for three days and nights. Väinämöinen drew his sword and struck at the fog, cleaving a path through it; the mist scattered and the boat went on. Next Louhi called up the sea monster Iku-Turso, which rose from the deep and raised great waves to overturn the boat. Väinämöinen seized the monster by the ears, lifted it out of the water and asked: 'Iku-Turso, why have you risen from the sea to bar our way?' He commanded it to sink back to the bottom and never again show itself to men, and it sank. Last, Louhi begged Ukko for a raging storm; the waves rose sky-high, the boat pitched and rolled, and a great wave swept Väinämöinen's beloved kantele overboard into the depths. Gazing at the sea he said sorrowfully: 'My joy has sunk into the sea, and I shall never find it again.' That harp was never found again; in a later rune Väinämöinen has to make another.

Evidence / 证据《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第四十二章。claim.v0350.kal_4.10
11

鹰形的洛希Louhi as an eagle

洛希造了一艘巨大的战船，让上百名武士带着刀剑和弓箭上船，亲自率领他们追赶。眼看就要追上了，她又变出了一个可怕的样子：她把镰刀装在脚上做爪子，把船身变成翅膀，变成一只巨大的鹰，一边翅膀上载着一百个武士，尾巴上载着一千个弓箭手，向英雄们的船扑来。万奈莫宁向乌戈祈祷，求乌戈保护他们。巨鹰落在船的桅杆上，船几乎被压翻。伊尔马里宁和勒明凯宁拔剑去砍，勒明凯宁砍下了鹰的几根羽毛。万奈莫宁从水里拔起船舵，用船舵狠狠地向巨鹰打去，打断了它的爪子，鹰爪纷纷掉进海里，只剩下一个小小的爪尖。洛希的武士们也纷纷从鹰的翅膀上跌落，掉进海里，就像秋天的树叶从树上落下来一样。这是《卡勒瓦拉》里最壮观的一场战斗：一边是变成巨鹰的北方女主人和她的大军，一边是一艘小船上的三位英雄。

Louhi built a great war-ship, put a hundred warriors aboard with swords, bows and arrows, and led the pursuit herself. When she was nearly upon them she took a terrible shape: she fixed scythes to her feet for talons, turned the ship into wings and became a giant eagle, carrying a hundred warriors on one wing and a thousand bowmen on her tail, and swooped down on the heroes' boat. Väinämöinen prayed to Ukko for protection. The giant eagle settled on the mast and nearly overturned the boat. Ilmarinen and Lemminkäinen struck at it with their swords; Lemminkäinen cut away a few of its feathers. Väinämöinen pulled the rudder from the water and struck the eagle hard with it, smashing its talons, which fell into the sea until only one small claw was left. Louhi's warriors fell from the eagle's wings into the sea like autumn leaves falling from a tree. It is the grandest battle in the Kalevala: on one side the mistress of the north turned giant eagle with her host, on the other three heroes in one small boat.

Evidence / 证据《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第四十三章。claim.v0350.kal_4.11
12

三宝的碎片The fragments of the Sampo

洛希虽然失去了爪子，却不肯罢休。她用仅剩的那根小小的爪尖——诗中说是她的小指——勾住了三宝，想把它从船上拖走。三宝从船上滑落，跌进了大海，在海中摔成了碎片。大块的碎片沉到了海底，从此大海有了取之不尽的财富，海里的鱼和宝藏都由此而来。小块的碎片随着波浪漂流，漂到了卡勒瓦拉的海岸上。万奈莫宁在岸边一块块地拾起这些碎片，把它们种进土里，祈求它们长出黑麦和大麦，带来丰收和富足。洛希只抢回了三宝那五彩的盖子，带回了波赫约拉，从此北方日渐贫穷。洛希在空中恶狠狠地发誓：我要给你们送去瘟疫，送去冰霜，送去猛兽，我还要把太阳和月亮偷走！万奈莫宁回答说：我不怕你的诅咒。他向乌戈祈祷，请乌戈保护卡勒瓦拉的人们，保护他们的田地和庄稼，让三宝的碎片永远给这片土地带来福祉。

Though she had lost her talons, Louhi would not give up. With the one small claw she had left — her little finger, the poem says — she hooked the Sampo and tried to drag it from the boat. The Sampo slipped from the boat, fell into the sea, and was shattered. The large pieces sank to the bottom, and from them the sea has its endless riches, its fish and its treasures. The small pieces drifted on the waves to the shores of Kalevala. Väinämöinen gathered them one by one on the beach, planted them in the earth, and prayed that they would bring forth rye and barley, plenty and prosperity. Louhi took home to Pohjola only the Sampo's many-coloured lid, and from then on the north grew poorer. From the air Louhi swore fiercely: 'I will send you plague and frost and wild beasts; I will steal the sun and the moon!' Väinämöinen answered that he did not fear her curses, and prayed to Ukko to protect the people of Kalevala, their fields and their crops, and to let the fragments of the Sampo bless the land for ever.

Evidence / 证据《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第四十三章。claim.v0350.kal_4.12
本系列已读完。This is the last part of the series.
Editorial boundary / 编辑边界

依据克劳福德 1888 年英译《卡勒瓦拉》第三十九至四十三章，按诗章顺序讲述。康特勒琴是芬兰的传统弹拨乐器，至今仍被视为民族象征；本篇讲述的是隆洛特编排的史诗文本。

印度教传统 / Hindu

摩诃婆罗多 · 第一部 那罗与达摩衍蒂Mahābhārata, Part 1: Nala and Damayantī

般度五子在掷骰中失去王国、流放森林，坚战悲叹世上没有比他更不幸的国王，仙人巨马就给他讲了那罗的故事。尼沙陀国王那罗与毗陀婆公主达摩衍蒂经天鹅传情而相爱。选婿大会上，因陀罗、阿耆尼、伐楼那和阎摩四位天神都化作那罗的模样，达摩衍蒂凭着天神不流汗、不眨眼、脚不沾地的特征认出了真正的那罗。迦利因此怀恨，等了十二年，趁那罗一次疏忽进入他的身体，让他在骰子上把王国输给了弟弟补湿迦罗。那罗与妻子流落森林，在半夜割下她的一半衣裳，丢下她独自离去。达摩衍蒂历经蟒蛇、猎人、商队和象群的灾难，到了车底国；那罗则从林火中救出蛇王迦尔郭吒迦，被它咬后变了模样，化名巴胡迦，做了阿逾陀王利图帕尔纳的车夫。达摩衍蒂宣布第二次选婿，利图帕尔纳乘巴胡迦驾的车一日飞驰百由旬，途中把骰子的学问教给了他，迦利从那罗身上离去。夫妻终于相认，那罗赢回了王国，宽恕了弟弟。

When the Pāṇḍavas have lost their kingdom at dice and gone into exile, Yudhiṣṭhira laments that no king was ever so unfortunate, and the sage Bṛhadaśva tells him the story of Nala. Nala, king of the Nishadhas, and Damayantī, princess of Vidarbha, fall in love through a swan's messages. At her svayaṃvara the gods Indra, Agni, Varuṇa and Yama all take Nala's form, but Damayantī knows the real Nala because the gods do not sweat or blink and their feet do not touch the ground. Kali resents it, waits twelve years for a lapse and enters Nala, who loses his kingdom at dice to his brother Pushkara. Exiled in the forest, Nala cuts away half of his sleeping wife's garment at midnight and leaves her. Damayantī survives a python, a hunter, a stampede of elephants and reaches the Chedi kingdom; Nala rescues the nāga Karkoṭaka from a forest fire, is bitten and changed, and becomes Bāhuka, charioteer to King Ṛtuparṇa of Ayodhyā. Damayantī announces a second svayaṃvara; Ṛtuparṇa races there with Bāhuka, teaching him the science of dice on the way, and Kali leaves Nala. Husband and wife know each other again, and Nala wins back his kingdom and forgives his brother.
